--- 
title: "Meet the WNBA"
format:
  dashboard:
    scrolling: true
    embed-resources: true
    # Only three chunks draw through a graphics device -- the charts answering
    # the crosstalk selection are plotly widgets, untouched by this. All three
    # are lines, dots and text, which vectorise small and stay sharp at any zoom,
    # where the default was a 2x raster: 619 KB of base64 becomes 270 KB.
    fig-format: svg
theme: styles.scss
# svglite rather than the `svg` device this format would otherwise pick, which is
# cairo and writes every glyph as a path -- 76 KB of outlines on a chart of
# twenty-two points, and not a `<text>` element in the file. svglite writes text
# as text.
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    dev: svglite
---


```{r packages}
# the figure device, named in this document's yaml. knitr only needs it
# installed, but renv's snapshot reads `library()` calls and nothing else, so
# without this line the lockfile does not know the render depends on it
library(svglite)
library(htmltools)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(wehoop)
library(ggrepel)
library(reactable)
library(purrr)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
# required by wehoop: pre-2024 season .rds files store their columns as arrow
# ALTREP vectors, which readRDS silently returns as length-zero vectors (and
# rbindlist then pads to NA) unless arrow is loaded
library(arrow)
```


```{r data}
this_year <- as.integer(year(now()))

seasons <- c(2004:as.integer(this_year))

# Load the configuration
config <- config::get()

# get data based on the configuration

if (config$data_source == "local") {
    dat <- readRDS("dat.rds")
    sched <- readRDS("sched.rds")
}
  
if (config$data_source == "wehoop") {
    dat <- load_wnba_player_box(seasons = seasons)
    sched <- wehoop::load_wnba_schedule(seasons = seasons)
}

# What part of the season a game belongs to, settled once for the whole
# document.
#
# `type_id` names a *round*, not a part of the season, and the playoff rounds
# only exist from 2019 on. Every playoff game from 2004 through 2018 -- and six
# of 2019's -- carries `type_id == 1` under `season_type == 3`, indistinguishable
# from a regular-season game by that column alone. This document read
# `type_id == 1` as "regular season" in twelve places, which folded 282 playoff
# games into every career total: Diana Taurasi showed 11,753 career points
# against the league's 10,646, Tina Charles 8,661 against 8,396.
#
# Neither column carries the answer on its own, so neither is asked for it
# again below.
sched <- sched |>
  mutate(
    game_kind = case_when(
      type_id == 4 ~ "allstar",
      type_id == 39 ~ "cup",
      season_type == 3 ~ "post",
      season_type == 2 & type_id == 1 ~ "regular",
      .default = "other"
    )
  )

sched_games <- sched |> 
  select(game_id, game_date, season_type, type_id, type_abbreviation, game_kind,
  home_display_name, home_score, away_display_name, away_score, attendance) |> 
    mutate(attendance = as.integer(attendance))

# game types
game_types <- sched_games |> 
  select(game_id, type_id, type_abbreviation, game_kind)

# Drop All-Star exhibition rosters, which are not real teams. This used to be
# `filter(team_id < 90)`, back when every franchise had a two-digit id and only
# the exhibition rosters did not. ESPN now issues six-digit ids to new
# franchises too, so that test also removed Golden State, Toronto and Portland.
# Exclude the exhibitions by game type instead, which is what was always meant.
dat <- dat |>
  left_join(game_types, by = "game_id") |>
  filter(game_kind != "allstar") |>
  # Drop players who dressed but did not play. ESPN carries a row per rostered
  # player per game; the inactive ones have no minutes and no stats, but they
  # still inflate every n_distinct(game_id) used as a games-played denominator.
  # That is what put this dashboard's per-game averages under ESPN's -- Caitlin
  # Clark sat 3 games, which read as 19.3 ppg here against ESPN's 21.5.
  #
  # The `did_not_play` flag only became reliable in 2013. Before that, 10-22%
  # of rows per season are inactive players it never marked; they show up as a
  # row with no minutes and every stat column NA. `!is.na(points)` catches
  # exactly those 7,654 rows and nothing else -- of 102,076 rows that do carry
  # minutes, not one is blank across all thirteen stat columns.
  #
  # Together these keep "one row = one game actually played" true downstream.
  filter(!(did_not_play %in% TRUE), !is.na(points)) |>
  # One career, one name. Every aggregation below groups by display name, so a
  # player who changed hers came out as two careers: Skylar Diggins-Smith with
  # 4,255 points and Skylar Diggins with 1,541, where the league lists a single
  # Skylar Diggins with 5,758. Six careers were split this way.
  #
  # This canonicalises the name rather than regrouping on `athlete_id`, because
  # grouping by id would break three careers that matching on name gets right:
  # ESPN issued two ids to one player for Li Yueru, Wendy Palmer and Isabel
  # Sanchez. Taking the most recent name each id used merges the splits and
  # leaves those three merged.
  #
  # It belongs here, once, because crosstalk keys and every lookup table further
  # down are keyed on the name string.
  mutate(
    athlete_display_name = if (is.na(athlete_id[1])) {
      athlete_display_name
    } else {
      athlete_display_name[which.max(game_date)]
    },
    .by = athlete_id
  )

games <- dat |>
  filter(season == this_year) |>
  summarise(
    team_1 = first(team_display_name),
    team_2 = first(opponent_team_display_name),
    .by = c(game_id, game_date)
  ) |> 
    arrange(desc(game_date))

# max number of games this year for any team
num_games <-dat |>
  filter(
    season == this_year,
    game_kind == "regular"
    ) |>
  select(team_display_name, game_id, game_date) |>
  unique() |> 
  arrange(team_display_name, desc(game_date)) |> 
  count(team_display_name, sort = TRUE) |> 
  head(1) |>
  pull(n)

```

```{r freshness}
#| output: asis

# The dashboard is rendered and published by hand, so it carries no other
# signal of how current it is. Report both dates: the render date alone would
# imply the data is as fresh as the render, which it is not.

fmt_date <- function(d) {
  d <- as.Date(d)
  paste0(format(d, "%b"), " ", as.integer(format(d, "%d")), ", ", format(d, "%Y"))
}

freshness_stamp <- paste0(
  "Data through ", fmt_date(max(dat$game_date, na.rm = TRUE)),
  "  ·  Rendered ", fmt_date(Sys.Date())
)

# The navbar is built by Quarto after this chunk runs, so append to it on load.
# The tab list carries Bootstrap's `me-auto`, which right-aligns any sibling
# placed after it.
cat(sprintf(
  '<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var nav = document.querySelector("#dashboard-collapse");
  if (!nav) return;
  var stamp = document.createElement("span");
  stamp.className = "navbar-stamp";
  stamp.textContent = "%s";
  nav.appendChild(stamp);
});
</script>',
  freshness_stamp
))
```

```{r funcs1}
player_stats <- function(
  data, season_part = c("regular", "post"), my_season = NULL
  ) {
  
  # stop if no game_kind column
  stopifnot("game_kind" %in% names(data))

  season_part <- match.arg(season_part)

  result <- data |> 
    filter(
      !is.na(athlete_display_name),
      game_kind == season_part
      )

  if (!is.null(my_season)) {
    result <- result |> 
      filter(season == my_season)
  }

  result <- result |>
    replace_na(list(points = 0)) |>
    summarise(
      position = paste(
        unique(athlete_position_name),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      total_games = if_else(
        nchar(n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE)) == 1,
        as.integer(paste0("0", n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE))),
        as.integer((n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE)))
      ),
      total_seasons = if_else(
        !is.null(my_season),
        1,
        as.integer(n_distinct(season, na.rm = TRUE))
      ),
      seasons = if_else(
        n_distinct(season, na.rm = TRUE) != 1,
        paste(range(season, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-"),
        as.character(range(season, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-")[[1]]
      ),
      # The club she played her most recent game for. `last()` would take the
      # last row of the group rather than the latest game, and `dat` does not
      # arrive sorted by date: that read the wrong club for 74 careers and for
      # 14 of this season's players -- Betnijah Laney-Hamilton showed as New
      # York when her last game was Washington's. It went unseen while this
      # column only sat on the season page; it is on both pages now.
      latest_team = team_display_name[which.max(game_date)],
      total_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
      ppg = list(points), # list for sparkline plots in table rows
      goals_made = sum(field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      threes_made = sum(three_point_field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      frees_made = sum(free_throws_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_assists = sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_rebounds = sum(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_steals = sum(steals, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_blocks = sum(blocks, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_turnovers = sum(turnovers, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_fouls = sum(fouls, na.rm = TRUE),
      total_ejections = sum(ejected, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    rename(
      athlete = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(total_points))

  if (!is.null(my_season)) {
    result |>
      select(-total_seasons)
  } else {
    result
  }
}

# player points per season over entire career
player_pps <- function(data, season_part = "regular") {

  data |>
    filter(game_kind == season_part) |>
    replace_na(list(points = 0)) |>
    summarise(
      points = as.integer(sum(points, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .by = c(athlete_display_name, season)
    ) |>
    arrange(athlete_display_name, season)
}
```

```{r funcs2}
player_doubles <- function(data, season_part = "regular", my_season = NULL) {
  dat <- data |>
    filter(game_kind == season_part)

  if (!is.null(my_season)) {
    dat <- dat %>%
      filter(season == my_season)
  }

  dat |>
    select(
      athlete = athlete_display_name,
      game_id,
      points,
      rebounds,
      assists,
      steals,
      blocks
    ) |>
    mutate(game_id = as.character(game_id)) |>
    arrange(game_id) |>
    mutate(
      across(
        points:blocks,
        \(x) if_else(is.na(x) | x < 10, FALSE, TRUE)
      )
    ) |>
    mutate(
      doubles = as.integer(
        rowSums(
          pick(where(
            ~ is.logical(.x)
          ))
        )
      )
    ) |>
    mutate(
      doubles_type = case_when(
        doubles == 2 ~ "double_double",
        doubles == 3 ~ "triple_double",
        doubles == 4 ~ "quadruple_double",
        doubles == 5 ~ "quintuple_double",
        .default = "other"
      )
    ) |>
    select(game_id, athlete, doubles_type) |>
    count(athlete, doubles_type) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = doubles_type,
      values_from = n
    ) |>
    replace_na(
      list(double_double = 0, triple_double = 0)
    ) |>
    mutate(
      double_double = if_else(
        triple_double > 0, double_double + triple_double, double_double
      )
    ) |>
    select(athlete, triple_double, double_double)
}
```

```{r funcs3}

stat <- function(data, col, ...) {
  if (n_distinct(data$seasons) > 1) {
    # A career leaderboard says how long she was at it -- how many seasons, and
    # which -- and then, like the season one, the two clubs that place her: the
    # franchise she last played for and the college she came up at.
    #
    # The club is headed "Team" here as it is on the season page, one word for
    # what is one column. It holds the club she last played for, which for a
    # finished career is where it ended rather than where it was made -- Tina
    # Thompson's four titles are Houston's, and this reads Seattle. The span
    # beside it is what says the row is a career and not a current club.
    data |>
      select(athlete, {{ col }}, total_seasons, seasons, latest_team, college) |>
      arrange(desc(.data[[col]])) |>
      slice(1:150) |>
      mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
      select(
        rank, athlete, {{ col }}, total_seasons, seasons, latest_team, college
      )
  } else if (n_distinct(data$seasons) == 1) {
    # One season, so the span is that season written out 150 times. The page
    # heading already carries the year; the column carried nothing.
    #
    # What it carries instead is what the total comes to a game, which is the
    # one that says whether a leader got there by being better or by being
    # available. A career leaderboard has no use for it -- a rate across
    # twenty seasons is an average of averages -- and carries the seasons and
    # the span in its place. Both pages name the two clubs.
    #
    # reactable takes its column order from the frame, so this select is where
    # the reading order is decided: who she is and what she did, then the two
    # clubs that are the context around it.
    data |>
      select(athlete, latest_team, college, total_games, {{ col }}) |>
      arrange(desc(.data[[col]])) |>
      slice(1:150) |>
      mutate(
        rank = row_number(),
        # `NULL` drops the column rather than creating it, which is what games
        # played wants: its own rate is 1 by construction.
        per_game = if (col == "total_games") NULL else .data[[col]] / total_games
      ) |>
      select(
        rank, athlete, {{ col }}, any_of("per_game"), latest_team, college
      )
  }
}
```

```{r helpers}
# ESPN serves headshots at 350px -- 290 KB each -- and crests at 500px, for
# pictures this page draws at 110px and 26px. Its own combiner endpoint resizes
# on the CDN and returns the same face at 13 KB. Nothing inlines these, so the
# full-size versions were a live request per player on every view.
# The combiner resizes to exactly the width and height asked for, without
# preserving aspect: a 600x436 headshot requested at 120x120 comes back
# squashed, which stretched every face in the comparison table. Ask for a width
# only and let it scale proportionally, or pass a height that matches the
# source's own ratio. CSS `object-fit: cover` does any cropping from there.
espn_img <- function(url, w, h = NULL) {
  path <- str_replace(url, "^https?://[a-z0-9.]+", "")
  size <- paste0("&w=", w, if (!is.null(h)) paste0("&h=", h))
  if_else(is.na(url), NA_character_, paste0(
    "https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=", path, size
  ))
}

# ESPN's brand colours are picked for white backgrounds, so several of them --
# Dallas navy, Indiana navy, Seattle green -- disappear against a dark page.
# Lift value and saturation to a floor so every franchise still reads as itself.
accent <- function(hex) {
  hex <- ifelse(is.na(hex) | hex == "", "f57b20", hex)
  map_chr(hex, function(h) {
    hsv_cols <- rgb2hsv(col2rgb(paste0("#", h)))
    v <- max(hsv_cols[3, 1], 0.62)
    s <- if (hsv_cols[2, 1] < 0.06) 0 else max(hsv_cols[2, 1], 0.42)
    hsv(hsv_cols[1, 1], s, v)
  })
}

pct_of <- function(made, att) if_else(att > 0, 100 * made / att, NA_real_)

fmt1 <- function(x) if_else(is.finite(x), sprintf("%.1f", x), "—")
fmt_pct <- function(x) if_else(is.finite(x), sprintf("%.1f%%", x), "—")

short_date <- function(d) {
  d <- as.Date(d)
  paste0(format(d, "%b"), " ", as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
```

```{r colleges}
# Where each player came up. Nothing in the box scores says so -- `dat` is a
# game log, and ESPN keeps a player's school on her athlete record instead --
# so it is asked for once per athlete and kept on disk, the way the franchise
# crests below are. A render with no network then costs nothing, and a
# mid-season signing costs one request.
#
# Every athlete in the record, not only this season's: the career leaderboards
# name the college too, and they reach back to 2004.
#
# A player with no college is cached as NA rather than left out of the cache.
# Two kinds of player have none, and only one of them is a gap.
#
# ESPN names a school for 687 of the 936 players in this record -- 83% of those
# still playing, 60% of those last seen before 2011, because its record of an
# old career thins out. That sounds worse than the page reads. The leaderboards
# show the top 150, and a career deep enough to reach one is a career ESPN kept:
# 142 of the 150 leading scorers have their school, and all eight who do not are
# Lauren Jackson, Penny Taylor, Emma Meesseman and the rest -- Australians,
# Belgians and Brazilians who came up through clubs and never attended a
# college. On the rows that show, a blank is the answer rather than a gap.
#
# Either way it is cached as NA, since asking again every render would only get
# the same blank back.
college_cache <- "colleges.rds"

all_athletes <- dat |>
  filter(!is.na(athlete_id)) |>
  distinct(athlete_id, athlete = athlete_display_name)

known_colleges <- if (file.exists(college_cache)) {
  readRDS(college_cache)
} else {
  tibble(athlete_id = integer(), college = character())
}

# httr rather than reading the URL straight into jsonlite, for the reason
# update_data.R gives at its own ESPN call: base R's url() connection sends a
# user agent ESPN answers with a 403.
espn_college <- function(id) {
  url <- paste0(
    "https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis/common/v3/sports/basketball/wnba",
    "/athletes/", id
  )

  # `terminate_on` because ESPN has no record at all for some of the older
  # careers and answers 404. RETRY treats any non-success as worth another go,
  # and backs off between them: retrying those turned a 30-second first render
  # into one that had not finished in two minutes.
  resp <- try(
    httr::RETRY("GET", url, times = 2, quiet = TRUE, terminate_on = c(200, 404)),
    silent = TRUE
  )

  # A 404 is ESPN's answer -- there is no record of this player -- so it is
  # cached as a blank like any other. Anything else is the network failing to
  # deliver an answer, so nothing is written and the next render asks again.
  if (inherits(resp, "try-error")) return(NULL)
  if (httr::status_code(resp) == 404) {
    return(tibble(athlete_id = id, college = NA_character_))
  }
  if (httr::status_code(resp) != 200) return(NULL)

  payload <- try(
    jsonlite::fromJSON(
      httr::content(resp, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
      simplifyVector = FALSE
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  if (inherits(payload, "try-error")) return(NULL)

  tibble(
    athlete_id = id,
    college = payload$athlete$college$name %||% NA_character_
  )
}

# Only whoever the cache has never been asked about. Anything that fails to
# arrive is simply not cached, so the column comes out blank for her this
# render and the next one asks again -- the same bargain the crests make.
unasked <- setdiff(all_athletes$athlete_id, known_colleges$athlete_id)

if (length(unasked) > 0) {
  fetched <- map(unasked, espn_college) |> list_rbind()
  if (nrow(fetched) > 0) {
    known_colleges <- bind_rows(known_colleges, fetched)
    saveRDS(known_colleges, college_cache)
  }
}

# One school per player, keyed on her display name: every table downstream is
# keyed that way, and ESPN issued two athlete ids to three of these careers
# (see the canonicalising `mutate` in the data chunk), which would otherwise
# put a player in a leaderboard twice.
player_college <- all_athletes |>
  left_join(known_colleges, by = "athlete_id") |>
  summarise(
    college = if (all(is.na(college))) NA_character_ else na.omit(college)[[1]],
    .by = athlete
  )
```

```{r dataprep-career}

pps <- dat |>
  player_pps() |>
  arrange(athlete_display_name, season) |>
  summarise(
    pps = list(points),
    # the years those points belong to. The dossier used to count its bars off
    # from the first year of the career span, which is a year short from the
    # first season a player missed onward: Taurasi sat out 2015, so her 2016
    # bar read 2015 and every bar after it was wrong too.
    pps_seasons = list(season),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  )

pdat_career <- player_stats(data = dat, season_part = "regular")

# Both sets of leaderboards name the college, so both frames carry it. A left
# join, so a player ESPN has no record of keeps her row and loses only the cell.
pdat_career <- pdat_career |>
  left_join(player_college, by = join_by(athlete))

player_seasons <- pdat_career |>
  select(athlete, total_games, total_seasons, seasons) |> 
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.double),
      as.integer
    )
  )

doubles_career <- dat |>
  player_doubles()

main_stats_career <- pdat_career |>
  select(
    athlete,
    total_points,
    # total_assists,
    # total_rebounds,
    # total_steals,
    # total_blocks,
    position,
    latest_team
  )

doubles_career <- doubles_career |>
  left_join(main_stats_career, by = join_by(athlete)) |>
  left_join(pps, by = join_by(athlete == athlete_display_name)) |>
  left_join(
    player_seasons,
    by = join_by(athlete)
  ) |>
  mutate(rookie = if_else(seasons == year(now()), "rookie", ""))  |> 
  arrange(desc(total_points)) |>
  # Where a career stands, settled here rather than counted down to. The
  # leaderboards have carried a rank column since they were written; the two
  # tables that open each page did not, so reading a row a hundred deep meant
  # counting rows to it.
  #
  # It ranks on points, because that is the order the frame is in, and it is
  # fixed at render time for the same reason the leaderboards' is: sorting the
  # table by another column leaves this reading points rank rather than row
  # position. A team filter leaves it non-contiguous, which is the point --
  # 3, 17, 44 says where those three stand in the league, where 1, 2, 3 would
  # only say they are the three.
  mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
  # reactable takes its column order from the frame, not from `columns`, so
  # this select is where the table's reading order is decided: where she ranks,
  # who she is, then what she scored, then the doubles she turned it into
  select(rank, athlete, rookie, total_points, triple_double, double_double, pps, everything())

# kept as a plain frame under its own name: the career panel behind an expanded
# row reads from it, and a SharedData wrapper has no columns to read
doubles_career_df <- doubles_career

doubles_career <- SharedData$new(doubles_career_df, group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

```

```{r dataprep-season}
pdat_season <- player_stats(data = dat, season_part = "regular", my_season = this_year)
doubles_season <- player_doubles(data = dat, my_season = this_year)

# as above, for the season leaderboards
pdat_season <- pdat_season |>
  left_join(player_college, by = join_by(athlete))

main_stats_season <- pdat_season |>
  select(
    athlete,
    total_points,
    ppg,
    # total_assists,
    # total_rebounds,
    # total_steals,
    # total_blocks,
    position,
    latest_team
  )

doubles_season <- doubles_season |>
  left_join(main_stats_season, by = join_by(athlete)) |>
  left_join(
    pdat_career |> select(athlete, seasons_played = seasons),
    by = join_by(athlete)
  ) |>
  mutate(rookie = if_else(seasons_played == year(now()), "rookie", ""))  |> 
  arrange(desc(total_points)) |>
  # as above: rank on points, fixed at render time
  mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
  # reactable takes its column order from the frame, not from `columns`, so
  # this select is where the table's reading order is decided: where she ranks,
  # who she is, then what she scored, then the doubles she turned it into
  select(rank, athlete, rookie, total_points, everything())

# as above: the player panel behind an expanded row needs the plain frame
doubles_season_df <- doubles_season

doubles_season <- SharedData$new(doubles_season_df, group = "experience", key = ~athlete)
```

```{r comparedata}
# How many games each team has played so far, which is the denominator in the
# league's own bar for a leaders list: 70% of team games played, or 525 points
# (https://stats.wnba.com/help/statminimums/). Named for what it counts, since
# `team_games` is a different frame in the standings below.
#
# The minimums are written per season and gate season leaders. They have no
# career equivalent and the league applies none to its all-time lists, so this
# qualifies the ranking on this page and nothing on the All Time one, where a
# career total is its own answer to the question a minimum asks.
team_games_played <- dat |>
  filter(season == this_year, game_kind == "regular") |>
  distinct(team_id, game_id) |>
  count(team_id, name = "team_games")

# per-game and percentage stats for the player comparison table;
# not a SharedData - selection drives column visibility via the JS below
compare_raw <- dat |>
  filter(
    season == this_year,
    game_kind == "regular",
    !is.na(athlete_display_name)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    # 120px for a 60px slot, so the portrait stays sharp on a retina screen
    headshot = espn_img(
      first(athlete_headshot_href[!is.na(athlete_headshot_href)]), 120
    ),
    # nickname rather than the full display name: it has to read under a 60px
    # photo, where "Golden State Valkyries" wraps to three lines
    team = team_name[which.max(game_date)],
    games = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    ppg = total_points / games,
    apg = sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
    rpg = sum(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
    spg = sum(steals, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
    bpg = sum(blocks, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
    topg = sum(turnovers, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
    fg_pct = 100 * sum(field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    tp_pct = 100 * sum(three_point_field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    ft_pct = 100 * sum(free_throws_made, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    # a player traded mid-season is measured against the team she is on now,
    # which is the nearest single reading of a rule written for a whole season
    team_id = team_id[which.max(game_date)],
    .by = athlete_display_name
  ) |>
  left_join(team_games_played, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(
    qualified = (games >= 0.7 * team_games) %in% TRUE | total_points >= 525
  )

photo_cell <- function(url, team) {
  portrait <- if_else(
    is.na(url),
    '<div style="width:60px;height:60px;border-radius:50%;background:#232732;margin:0 auto;"></div>',
    paste0(
      '<img src="', url, '" width="60" height="60" alt="" ',
      'style="width:60px;height:60px;border-radius:50%;object-fit:cover;background:#232732;" loading="lazy">'
    )
  )

  paste0(
    '<div class="compare-photo">',
    portrait,
    '<div class="compare-team">', coalesce(team, "&mdash;"), '</div>',
    "</div>"
  )
}

# column order is fixed at render time, so arranging by ppg here keeps any
# selection of columns sorted left-to-right by descending points per game
compare_wide <- compare_raw |>
  arrange(desc(ppg)) |>
  transmute(
    athlete = athlete_display_name,
    Photo = photo_cell(headshot, team),
    `Points / Game` = fmt1(ppg),
    `Assists / Game` = fmt1(apg),
    `Rebounds / Game` = fmt1(rpg),
    `Steals / Game` = fmt1(spg),
    `Blocks / Game` = fmt1(bpg),
    `Turnovers / Game` = fmt1(topg),
    `FG%` = fmt_pct(fg_pct),
    `3P%` = fmt_pct(tp_pct),
    `FT%` = fmt_pct(ft_pct),
    `FT Attempted` = as.character(fta)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-athlete, names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") |>
  # the headshots need no row label; "Photo" only stated the obvious. The name
  # has to survive as a column above so pivot_longer has something to key on.
  mutate(stat = if_else(stat == "Photo", "", stat)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = athlete, values_from = value)

compare_players <- setdiff(names(compare_wide), "stat")

# The columns the table opens on: the twenty best per game among the players
# who have qualified. Points per game cannot rank a league on its own -- it
# would seat a player with two big nights off the bench ahead of everyone --
# so it needs a field to choose from. This used to draw that field as the top
# fifty by total points, a stand-in for a qualifying rule. The league publishes
# the rule itself, so the stand-in is gone and `qualified` above carries it:
# 70% of her team's games, or 525 points.
#
# No reordering is needed here: `compare_wide` is already in descending
# points-per-game order, and a subset of a sorted list is sorted. It also still
# carries every player, so those who have not qualified -- and everyone below
# them -- stay reachable by selecting them in the left table.
compare_default <- compare_raw |>
  filter(qualified) |>
  arrange(desc(ppg)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  pull(athlete_display_name)

# crosstalk selection keys are athlete names, which are exactly the
# compare-table column ids, so no key-to-column mapping is needed
compare_js <- paste0(
  "(function() {\n",
  "  var players = ", jsonlite::toJSON(compare_players), ";\n",
  "  var defaults = ", jsonlite::toJSON(compare_default), ";\n",
  "  var clearBtn = null;\n",
  "  var selKeys = null;\n",
  "  var filtKeys = null;\n",
  "  function active() {\n",
  "    return !!((selKeys && selKeys.length) || (filtKeys && filtKeys.length));\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  // Three rungs, narrowest first: the players picked, else the team being\n",
  "  // filtered to, else the columns this table opens on.\n",
  "  function apply() {\n",
  "    var shown = (selKeys && selKeys.length) ? selKeys\n",
  "      : ((filtKeys && filtKeys.length) ? filtKeys : defaults);\n",
  "    var hidden = players.filter(function(p) { return shown.indexOf(p) === -1; });\n",
  "    if (window.Reactable) { Reactable.setHiddenColumns('compare-table', hidden); }\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  function showClear(active) {\n",
  "    if (clearBtn) { clearBtn.hidden = !active; }\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  // Why this exists: a selection and a team filter both narrow every page,\n",
  "  // and either can narrow one to nothing. Pick a career with no season this\n",
  "  // year -- Sue Bird, last season 2022 -- and the current-year page has no\n",
  "  // row left to untick, so the way out cannot be inside a table.\n",
  "  //\n",
  "  // Why the navbar: it used to be a button in each player table's card\n",
  "  // header, one per page, which worked but put a document-wide control in\n",
  "  // the chrome of one card on it -- and moved it as you walked between\n",
  "  // pages, to a header belonging to a table that is not the only thing being\n",
  "  // filtered. What it clears follows you from page to page, so it lives\n",
  "  // where the page numbers do: one button, one place, shown only when there\n",
  "  // is something to clear.\n",
  "  function buildClear(handle) {\n",
  "    var nav = document.getElementById('dashboard-collapse');\n",
  "    if (!nav) { return null; }\n",
  "    var btn = document.createElement('button');\n",
  "    btn.type = 'button';\n",
  "    btn.className = 'navbar-clear';\n",
  "    btn.textContent = '\\u2715 Clear';\n",
  "    btn.title = 'Clear the selection and the team filter';\n",
  "    btn.hidden = true;\n",
  "    // A handle can only clear its own contribution to the group's filter,\n",
  "    // and the team filter belongs to the standings script -- so ask that\n",
  "    // script to drop it rather than reaching for a handle that cannot.\n",
  "    btn.addEventListener('click', function() {\n",
  "      handle.set(null);\n",
  "      document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('wnba:clear-filter'));\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    // Before the freshness stamp, so the stamp -- which never changes and\n",
  "    // never moves -- keeps the right edge, and the button grows leftward into\n",
  "    // the empty middle rather than shoving it. `insertBefore` with a null\n",
  "    // reference appends, which is what should happen if the stamp is missing.\n",
  "    nav.insertBefore(btn, nav.querySelector('.navbar-stamp'));\n",
  "    return btn;\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  window.addEventListener('load', function() {\n",
  "    var handle = new crosstalk.SelectionHandle('experience');\n",
  "    // Listen-only: this handle never sets a filter, so it adds no constraint\n",
  "    // of its own to the group. It is here to hear the team filter change.\n",
  "    var filter = new crosstalk.FilterHandle('experience');\n",
  "    clearBtn = buildClear(handle);\n",
  "    handle.on('change', function(e) {\n",
  "      // Deselecting the last row broadcasts [], which plotly ignores entirely.\n",
  "      // TraceManager.prototype.updateSelection, in plotly's htmlwidget JS,\n",
  "      // restores origOpacity only on `keys === null`, and takes the highlight\n",
  "      // path only on `keys.length >= 1`. An empty array falls between the two\n",
  "      // branches, so every chart keeps the dim from the selection just cleared\n",
  "      // with nothing lit against it. A strict null is what restores them.\n",
  "      if (e.value && e.value.length === 0) { handle.set(null); return; }\n",
  "      selKeys = e.value;\n",
  "      apply();\n",
  "      showClear(active());\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    filter.on('change', function(e) {\n",
  "      filtKeys = e.value;\n",
  "      apply();\n",
  "      showClear(active());\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    selKeys = handle.value;\n",
  "    filtKeys = filter.filteredKeys;\n",
  "    apply();\n",
  "    showClear(active());\n",
  "  });\n",
  "})();"
)
```

```{r profiles}
# One row per player this season, carrying everything the panel behind an
# expanded table row shows. The tables themselves stay as they were; this is
# the detail that used to have nowhere to live.
season_box <- dat |>
  filter(season == this_year, game_kind == "regular", !is.na(athlete_display_name))

profile <- season_box |>
  summarise(
    shot = espn_img(first(na.omit(athlete_headshot_href)), 220),
    logo = espn_img(last(na.omit(team_logo)), 52),
    color = accent(team_color[which.max(game_date)]),
    team = team_display_name[which.max(game_date)],
    pos = first(na.omit(athlete_position_abbreviation)),
    jersey = first(na.omit(athlete_jersey)),
    g = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    mins = sum(minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    pts = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    reb = sum(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE),
    ast = sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE),
    stl = sum(steals, na.rm = TRUE),
    blk = sum(blocks, na.rm = TRUE),
    fgm = sum(field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
    fga = sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    tpm = sum(three_point_field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
    tpa = sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    ftm = sum(free_throws_made, na.rm = TRUE),
    fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  ) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  mutate(
    mpg = mins / g, ppg = pts / g, rpg = reb / g,
    apg = ast / g, spg = stl / g, bpg = blk / g,
    fgp = pct_of(fgm, fga), tpp = pct_of(tpm, tpa), ftp = pct_of(ftm, fta),
    # counts a three as three points and includes free throws, so it measures
    # efficiency across every kind of shot. The 0.44 estimates how many free
    # throws end a possession.
    ts = pct_of(pts, 2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta))
  )

# One bar per game on her team's schedule, in date order -- not one per game
# she played in. A log of only her own appearances is the same shape whichever
# way her season has gone, and reading two cards against each other says
# nothing, because 22 bars and 34 bars are drawn at the same width. Against the
# whole 44-game schedule, the games she missed are the gaps and the season left
# to play is the tail.
#
# One row per team per game. The postponed game is dropped: it is on the
# schedule twice, once on the date it was called off and once on the date it
# was replayed, and only the second is a game. Dropping it leaves all fifteen
# teams on exactly 44.
season_schedule <- sched |>
  filter(
    season == this_year,
    game_kind == "regular",
    status_type_name != "STATUS_POSTPONED"
  )

team_slots <- bind_rows(
  season_schedule |>
    transmute(
      game_id, game_date,
      team_id = as.integer(home_id), opp = away_abbreviation
    ),
  season_schedule |>
    transmute(
      game_id, game_date,
      team_id = as.integer(away_id), opp = home_abbreviation
    )
)

# Which of those games have been played, taken from the box scores rather than
# from the schedule's own status. The status flag lags the scores it sits
# beside: on 2026-08-15 it still called 38 games scheduled that had been
# played, the whole fortnight from August 2nd on, which would have drawn a
# fortnight of finished basketball as a season still to come.
# named for what it marks rather than for what it counts: `team_games` is a
# different frame in the standings below, built on different columns
team_slots_played <- season_box |>
  distinct(team_id, game_id, team_winner) |>
  mutate(team_played = TRUE)

# Whose season to measure a player against, on any given date: the team she
# last appeared for, and before her first appearance the team she first
# appeared for. 216 of this season's 228 players never left a team and take
# their one team's schedule; the twelve who moved are split at the date they
# moved. Without the split a traded player would be handed both teams' seasons
# and read as having missed half of each.
#
# Dates come from the schedule for slots and appearances alike, so the two are
# ordered on one clock.
appearances <- season_box |>
  distinct(athlete = athlete_display_name, game_id, played_team = team_id) |>
  inner_join(distinct(team_slots, game_id, game_date), by = "game_id") |>
  distinct(athlete, game_date, played_team)

season_slots <- appearances |>
  distinct(athlete, team_id = played_team) |>
  inner_join(team_slots, by = "team_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  left_join(appearances, by = c("athlete", "game_date")) |>
  arrange(athlete, game_date) |>
  group_by(athlete) |>
  fill(played_team, .direction = "downup") |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(team_id == played_team)

# Three states, and the two joins that separate them. `dat` was filtered up top
# to rows where a player actually played, so a slot with no box score behind it
# is one she was not in; whether her team has played it yet says which kind of
# absence it is.
game_log <- season_slots |>
  left_join(
    season_box |>
      transmute(
        athlete = athlete_display_name,
        game_id,
        p = as.integer(replace_na(points, 0))
      ),
    by = c("athlete", "game_id")
  ) |>
  left_join(team_slots_played, by = c("team_id", "game_id")) |>
  arrange(athlete, game_date) |>
  transmute(
    athlete,
    d = short_date(game_date),
    opp,
    p,
    won = team_winner %in% TRUE,
    state = case_when(
      !is.na(p) ~ "played",
      team_played %in% TRUE ~ "missed",
      .default = "to come"
    )
  ) |>
  nest(log = c(d, opp, p, won, state))

profile <- profile |> left_join(game_log, by = "athlete")

# indexed by name, so the panel builder is a lookup rather than a filter
profile_by <- split(profile, profile$athlete)

# the athlete's name behind her franchise's crest, so a table of names is also
# a table of teams without spending a column on it
crest_cell <- function(name) {
  p <- profile_by[[name]]
  logo <- if (is.null(p) || is.na(p$logo)) NULL else {
    tags$img(
      src = p$logo, alt = "", width = 18, height = 18, loading = "lazy",
      style = "flex:0 0 18px;object-fit:contain"
    )
  }
  div(
    style = "display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px",
    logo,
    span(style = "white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis", name)
  )
}

stat_cell <- function(k, v, lead = FALSE) {
  div(
    class = "dsr-stat",
    span(class = "dsr-k", k),
    span(class = if (lead) "dsr-v lead" else "dsr-v", v)
  )
}

# The panel Quarto opens under an expanded row. Built with htmltools rather
# than pasted strings, so the markup cannot come out unbalanced.
dossier <- function(name) {
  p <- profile_by[[name]]
  if (is.null(p)) {
    return(div(class = "dossier", div(class = "dsr-body", "No games this season.")))
  }

  gl <- p$log[[1]]
  top <- max(gl$p, 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Height means points and nothing else, so only a game she played has one.
  # The other two states are about the slot rather than about a score and take
  # the full height of the row: black where the game was played without her,
  # an empty outline where it has not been played at all. A missed game carries
  # the team's result, which is the one thing there is to say about a game she
  # was not in.
  bars <- pmap(
    list(gl$p, gl$won, gl$d, gl$opp, gl$state),
    \(p_, won_, d_, o_, s_) switch(
      s_,
      played = div(
        class = "dsr-bar",
        style = paste0("height:", max(round(100 * p_ / top), 3), "%"),
        title = paste0(d_, " vs ", o_, ": ", p_, " pts", if (won_) " (W)" else " (L)")
      ),
      missed = div(
        class = "dsr-bar missed",
        title = paste0(
          d_, " vs ", o_, ": missed",
          if (won_) " (team won)" else " (team lost)"
        )
      ),
      div(
        class = "dsr-bar to-come",
        title = paste0(d_, " vs ", o_, ": still to come")
      )
    )
  )

  div(
    class = "dossier",
    style = paste0("--team:", p$color),
    div(
      class = "dsr-id",
      if (is.na(p$shot)) NULL else tags$img(class = "dsr-shot", src = p$shot, alt = "", loading = "lazy"),
      div(class = "dsr-name", name),
      div(
        class = "dsr-meta",
        paste(
          c(if (!is.na(p$jersey)) paste0("#", p$jersey), p$pos, p$team),
          collapse = " · "
        )
      )
    ),
    div(
      class = "dsr-body",
      div(
        class = "dsr-grid",
        stat_cell("Games", p$g),
        stat_cell("Min/G", fmt1(p$mpg)),
        stat_cell("Pts/G", fmt1(p$ppg), lead = TRUE),
        stat_cell("Reb/G", fmt1(p$rpg)),
        stat_cell("Ast/G", fmt1(p$apg)),
        stat_cell("Stl/G", fmt1(p$spg)),
        stat_cell("Blk/G", fmt1(p$bpg)),
        stat_cell("FG%", fmt_pct(p$fgp)),
        stat_cell("3P%", fmt_pct(p$tpp)),
        stat_cell("FT%", fmt_pct(p$ftp)),
        stat_cell("TS%", fmt_pct(p$ts))
      ),
      # Two lines by hand. The panel is as wide as the table, which is a little
      # wider than the card it sits in, so a caption left to wrap on its own
      # breaks past the right edge and loses a word or two into the overflow.
      #
      # The counts are read off the states rather than written as "30 of 44",
      # which would put the ten games nobody has played yet on the same footing
      # as the four she missed. A state with nothing in it drops out of the
      # sentence, so the last week of the season does not read "0 to come".
      div(
        class = "dsr-logtitle",
        paste0(
          "Points, game by game — ",
          paste(
            # `c()` drops the NULLs, so an empty state leaves no comma behind
            c(
              paste(sum(gl$state == "played"), "played"),
              if (any(gl$state == "missed")) {
                paste(sum(gl$state == "missed"), "missed")
              },
              if (any(gl$state == "to come")) {
                paste(sum(gl$state == "to come"), "to come")
              }
            ),
            collapse = ", "
          ),
          "."
        ),
        tags$br(),
        paste0("Best night ", top, ". Black is missed, hollow still to come.")
      ),
      div(class = "dsr-log", bars)
    )
  )
}
```

```{r career-panel}
# The All Time table's panel. Career totals come from `pdat_career`, and the bars are
# `pps` -- points per season -- which was already computed for a sparkline and
# is reused here at a size worth reading.
career_by <- split(pdat_career, pdat_career$athlete)
pps_by <- split(pps, pps$athlete_display_name)

career_dossier <- function(name) {
  c_ <- career_by[[name]]
  if (is.null(c_)) {
    return(div(class = "dossier", div(class = "dsr-body", "No regular-season games.")))
  }

  # active players get their current crest and portrait; everyone else has none
  # in this data, and an empty slot is better than another player's face
  p <- profile_by[[name]]
  seasons_pts <- pps_by[[name]]$pps[[1]]
  bar_years <- pps_by[[name]]$pps_seasons[[1]]
  top <- max(seasons_pts, 1)

  bars <- imap(
    seasons_pts,
    \(v, i) div(
      class = "dsr-bar won",
      style = paste0("height:", max(round(100 * v / top), 3), "%"),
      title = paste0(bar_years[[i]], ": ", v, " pts")
    )
  )

  div(
    class = "dossier",
    style = paste0("--team:", if (is.null(p)) "#f57b20" else p$color),
    div(
      class = "dsr-id",
      if (is.null(p) || is.na(p$shot)) NULL else {
        tags$img(class = "dsr-shot", src = p$shot, alt = "", loading = "lazy")
      },
      div(class = "dsr-name", name),
      div(class = "dsr-meta", paste(c_$seasons, "·", c_$latest_team))
    ),
    div(
      class = "dsr-body",
      div(
        class = "dsr-grid",
        stat_cell("Seasons", c_$total_seasons),
        stat_cell("Games", format(c_$total_games, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Points", format(c_$total_points, big.mark = ","), lead = TRUE),
        stat_cell("Pts/G", fmt1(c_$total_points / c_$total_games)),
        stat_cell("Rebounds", format(c_$total_rebounds, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Assists", format(c_$total_assists, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Steals", format(c_$total_steals, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Blocks", format(c_$total_blocks, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Threes", format(c_$threes_made, big.mark = ",")),
        stat_cell("Turnovers", format(c_$total_turnovers, big.mark = ","))
      ),
      div(
        class = "dsr-logtitle",
        paste0("Points by season, best ", format(top, big.mark = ","))
      ),
      div(class = "dsr-log", bars)
    )
  )
}
```

```{r standings-prep}
# `sched.rds` has been loaded on every render and never displayed. One card per
# franchise: record, points for and against, and the last ten results.
team_games <- season_box |>
  distinct(game_id, game_date, team_abbreviation, team_display_name,
           team_color, team_logo, team_winner, team_score, opponent_team_score,
           # the tiebreak below has to know who each result came against
           opponent_team_abbreviation)

record <- team_games |>
  arrange(game_date) |>
  summarise(
    name = last(team_display_name),
    # The cards are a strip read across now rather than a rail read down, and a
    # strip is priced in width: "Golden State Valkyries" is half again as wide
    # as "Golden State", and the crest sitting beside it has already said which
    # club. Every name the league issues is a place and a one-word nickname, so
    # the nickname is the last word. `name` stays alongside -- it is what the
    # selection script matches the tables against, and what the card says on
    # hover.
    city = str_remove(last(team_display_name), "\\s+\\S+$"),
    color = accent(last(team_color)),
    logo = espn_img(last(team_logo), 52),
    w = sum(team_winner %in% TRUE),
    l = sum(team_winner %in% FALSE),
    pf = mean(team_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    pa = mean(opponent_team_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    form = list(tail(if_else(team_winner %in% TRUE, "w", "l"), 10)),
    .by = team_abbreviation
  )

# Teams level on winning percentage used to be left to `arrange`, which sorts
# stably and so handed the tie to whichever team's rows came first -- that is,
# to the order the season opened in. On 2026-08-14 it put Indiana above Atlanta
# at 21-12 apiece, against the league's own order, for no better reason than
# that Indiana appeared eighth in the opening weekend's box scores and Atlanta
# eleventh. The `desc(w)` that followed was wrong on its own terms too: it
# ranked 22-11 above 20-10, but those are one winning percentage and the league
# sends them to the tiebreak together.
#
# The league breaks a tie with, in order: (1) the better record in the games
# among the tied teams, (2) the better winning percentage against every team
# finishing .500 or better, (3) the better point differential in those same
# games among the tied teams, and (4) the better point differential across all
# games. The moment a criterion separates anyone, the procedure restarts at (1)
# on each part it leaves behind.
#
# Two of the four read differently before the season ends, and one cannot be
# read at all until it has.
#
# (2) is defined on ".500 or better record at the end of the season", so it has
# no answer until the season has an end. Mid-season the set of .500-or-better
# teams turns over almost nightly, and a card that moved because some third team
# lost would be a shift nothing on this page explains. It joins the procedure on
# the day the schedule runs out, which is the day the order it settles starts
# settling playoff seeding.
#
# (4) is written as a net total, "total points scored less total points allowed
# against all opponents". That is the right reading of a finished season, where
# every team has played the same 44 games. In August they have not, and a net
# total would reward whoever has played more, so until the season ends it is
# read per game. The two readings order a finished season identically.

# Whether the regular season has finished. `season_schedule` is this year's
# regular-season games with the postponement dropped, so every row in it is a
# game that gets played.
# Schedule status can lag a complete box score. On September 24, 2026, five
# finished games still said STATUS_SCHEDULED. A game with a box score has been
# played, regardless of that stale flag.
season_complete <- all(season_schedule$game_id %in% season_box$game_id)

# Two numbers that mean the same thing have to compare equal, or the teams
# holding them never get compared at all: .667 reached as 20-10 and as 22-11 is
# one winning percentage, and a differential is a mean of integers. Ten digits
# is far past any distinction a season under 100 games can draw.
level <- function(x) round(as.numeric(x), 10)

# The games a set of teams played against each other, and nothing else.
#
# `margin` is the net the rule asks for rather than a mean, which is what lets
# (3) speak for a team that has not met the others yet. Total points scored less
# total points allowed comes to zero over no games, where a winning percentage
# over no games is not a number at all. Within a tied group the counts are close
# enough that the objection to a net in (4) does not arise, and once the season
# is complete every team has met every other and the question is moot.
among <- function(teams) {
  team_games |>
    filter(team_abbreviation %in% teams,
           opponent_team_abbreviation %in% teams) |>
    summarise(
      pct = mean(team_winner %in% TRUE),
      margin = sum(team_score - opponent_team_score),
      .by = team_abbreviation
    )
}

# Every team that finished .500 or better, which (2) measures the tied teams
# against. Read off the same records the cards carry, so the criterion cannot
# disagree with the column beside it.
above_500 <- record |>
  filter(level(w / (w + l)) >= 0.5) |>
  pull(team_abbreviation)

against_500 <- function(teams) {
  team_games |>
    filter(team_abbreviation %in% teams,
           opponent_team_abbreviation %in% above_500) |>
    summarise(pct = mean(team_winner %in% TRUE), .by = team_abbreviation) |>
    score_of("pct", teams)
}

# One number per team, in the order asked for. `fill` is what a team with no row
# in `d` takes: zero where the criterion's own arithmetic comes to zero over no
# games, and NA where the criterion cannot speak for that team at all. An NA is
# what stops a criterion from ranking anybody, because a team it cannot place is
# a team the tie cannot eliminate.
score_of <- function(d, col, teams, fill = NA_real_) {
  out <- set_names(d[[col]], d$team_abbreviation)[teams]
  out[is.na(out)] <- fill
  out
}

# Point differential against all opponents. `record` carries pf and pa as means
# for the cards, so both readings are taken from the games instead.
season_diff <- team_games |>
  summarise(
    net = sum(team_score - opponent_team_score),
    per_game = mean(team_score - opponent_team_score),
    .by = team_abbreviation
  )

season_margin <- set_names(
  if (season_complete) season_diff$net else season_diff$per_game,
  season_diff$team_abbreviation
)

# higher is better in all four. (2) sits out until the season it is defined on
# has one to be defined on.
criteria <- c(
  list(\(teams) score_of(among(teams), "pct", teams)),
  if (season_complete) list(against_500),
  list(\(teams) score_of(among(teams), "margin", teams, fill = 0)),
  list(\(teams) season_margin[teams])
)

rank_tie <- function(teams) {
  if (length(teams) < 2) return(teams)

  for (criterion in criteria) {
    score <- level(criterion(teams))
    # Only (1) can still hand back an NA, and only before the season ends: a
    # team that has not met the others has no head-to-head winning percentage,
    # and ranking the teams that have met would eliminate nobody from the tie,
    # since the unplaced team could belong anywhere among them.
    if (anyNA(score) || n_distinct(score) == 1) next

    return(
      tibble(team = teams, score = score) |>
        arrange(desc(score)) |>
        # whoever is still level with a neighbour goes back through the whole
        # procedure together, from the first criterion. The group is smaller
        # now, and (1) recomputed among fewer teams can order it differently --
        # which is why this recurses instead of sorting on a list of keys.
        summarise(team = list(rank_tie(team)), .by = score) |>
        pull(team) |>
        unlist()
    )
  }

  # nothing in the procedure separates them; alphabetical at least gives the
  # same answer on every render
  sort(teams)
}

order_of_finish <- record |>
  mutate(pct = level(w / (w + l))) |>
  arrange(desc(pct)) |>
  summarise(team = list(rank_tie(team_abbreviation)), .by = pct) |>
  pull(team) |>
  unlist()

# back to the ten columns the cards are drawn from, in the order just settled
standings <- record |>
  arrange(match(team_abbreviation, order_of_finish))
```

```{r champions-prep}
# Every title since 2004, off the schedule that has been loaded on every render
# and never displayed. `type_id == 17` (FINAL) only exists from 2019 on; before
# that the finals carry season_type 3 with type_id 1 and the round is named
# only in the headline, so both paths are needed to reach all 22 seasons.
finals <- sched |>
  filter(
    game_kind == "post",
    status_type_completed %in% TRUE,
    type_id == 17 |
      str_detect(toupper(coalesce(notes_headline, "")), "WNBA FINALS|^FINALS")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    winner = if_else(home_winner %in% TRUE, home_display_name, away_display_name)
  )

# The chart these now mark runs back to 1997 and the schedule starts in 2004,
# so the league's first seven titles are typed out for the same reason the
# franchise eras are: they are older than the evidence. The gate in
# `franchise-prep` puts every title on a franchise era that was playing that
# season, so a name typed wrong here fails the render rather than sitting here
# wrong.
early_titles <- tribble(
  ~season,  ~champion,
  1997L, "Houston Comets",
  1998L, "Houston Comets",
  1999L, "Houston Comets",
  2000L, "Houston Comets",
  2001L, "Los Angeles Sparks",
  2002L, "Los Angeles Sparks",
  2003L, "Detroit Shock"
)

# The winner of the last game played is the champion only once the series is
# over. Mid-series it is just whoever won last: a Finals tied 3-3 would crown the
# team that tied it. So a title waits for the wins the format required: best of
# three in 2004, best of five through 2024, best of seven since.
finals_wins_needed <- function(season) {
  case_when(season >= 2025 ~ 4L, season >= 2005 ~ 3L, .default = 2L)
}

champions <- finals |>
  arrange(season, game_date) |>
  summarise(
    champion = last(winner),
    wins = sum(winner == last(winner)),
    .by = season
  ) |>
  filter(wins >= finals_wins_needed(season)) |>
  select(-wins) |>
  bind_rows(early_titles) |>
  arrange(desc(season)) |>
  # A card carries the franchise's current name; the schedule carries the name
  # it won under. Detroit Shock is Dallas Wings now, so its two titles light
  # that card. Sacramento Monarchs folded in 2009 and has no card, so 2005
  # lights for nobody -- right, not a gap.
  mutate(
    franchise = coalesce(
      unname(c("Detroit Shock" = "Dallas Wings")[champion]),
      champion
    )
  )

# The wins rule above drops a season whose finals games are missing from the
# schedule, and a title has to fail the render rather than quietly disappear.
stopifnot(
  "a finished season has no champion" =
    all(1997:(this_year - 1L) %in% champions$season)
)
```

```{r standings-js}
# Crosstalk selection keys are athlete names and each card carries its team
# display name in `data-team`; this map is the bridge between the two. Built
# from the current-season frame, so selecting an All Time player with no season
# this year lights no card - correct, since her franchise may not be playing.
player_team <- dat |>
  filter(season == this_year, game_kind %in% c("regular", "post")) |>
  arrange(game_date) |>
  summarise(latest_team = last(team_display_name), .by = athlete_display_name) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  filter(!is.na(latest_team))

player_team <- setNames(as.list(player_team$latest_team), player_team$athlete)

# and the inverse, which is what a card hands to the filter handle: clicking a
# team filters the group to that team's keys, so the roster *is* the filter
team_roster <- split(names(player_team), unlist(player_team))

standings_js <- paste0(
  "(function() {\n",
  "  var teamOf = ", jsonlite::toJSON(player_team, auto_unbox = TRUE), ";\n",
  "  var rosterOf = ", jsonlite::toJSON(team_roster), ";\n",
  "  var reduced = window.matchMedia\n",
  "    ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches\n",
  "    : false;\n",
  "  function teamsOf(keys) {\n",
  "    var out = {};\n",
  "    (keys || []).forEach(function(k) {\n",
  "      if (teamOf[k]) { out[teamOf[k]] = true; }\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    return out;\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  // Removing the class is not enough to replay the animation; the browser\n",
  "  // only restarts it after the element has been reflowed without it.\n",
  "  function bounce(card) {\n",
  "    card.classList.remove('is-bounce');\n",
  "    void card.offsetWidth;\n",
  "    card.classList.add('is-bounce');\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  // The strip scrolls sideways, so a lit card can be off either end of it.\n",
  "  // scrollIntoView would walk every scrollable ancestor and move the whole\n",
  "  // dashboard; measuring against the strip's own rect keeps the scroll in it.\n",
  "  function reveal(card, grid) {\n",
  "    var c = card.getBoundingClientRect();\n",
  "    var g = grid.getBoundingClientRect();\n",
  "    var delta = 0;\n",
  "    if (c.left < g.left) { delta = c.left - g.left - 6; }\n",
  "    else if (c.right > g.right) { delta = c.right - g.right + 6; }\n",
  "    if (!delta) { return; }\n",
  "    grid.scrollTo({\n",
  "      left: grid.scrollLeft + delta,\n",
  "      behavior: reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth'\n",
  "    });\n",
  "  }\n",
  "  window.addEventListener('load', function() {\n",
  "    var grid = document.getElementById('standings');\n",
  "    if (!grid) { return; }\n",
  "    var cards = Array.prototype.slice.call(\n",
  "      grid.querySelectorAll('.tcard')\n",
  "    );\n",
  "    cards.forEach(function(card) {\n",
  "      card.addEventListener('animationend', function() {\n",
  "        card.classList.remove('is-bounce');\n",
  "      });\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    var prev = [];\n",
  "    var handle = new crosstalk.SelectionHandle('experience');\n",
  "    function apply(value) {\n",
  "      var keys = value || [];\n",
  "      var added = keys.filter(function(k) { return prev.indexOf(k) === -1; });\n",
  "      prev = keys.slice();\n",
  "      var lit = teamsOf(keys);\n",
  "      var grew = teamsOf(added);\n",
  "      var first = null;\n",
  "      cards.forEach(function(card) {\n",
  "        var team = card.getAttribute('data-team');\n",
  "        var was = card.classList.contains('is-selected');\n",
  "        if (!lit[team]) { card.classList.remove('is-selected'); return; }\n",
  "        card.classList.add('is-selected');\n",
  "        // an already-lit card cannot light further, so a second player from\n",
  "        // the same team gets the bounce instead of a state change\n",
  "        if (was) { if (grew[team]) { bounce(card); } }\n",
  "        else if (!first) { first = card; }\n",
  "      });\n",
  "      if (first) { reveal(first, grid); }\n",
  "    }\n",
  "    handle.on('change', function(e) { apply(e.value); });\n",
  "    apply(handle.value);\n",
  "\n",
  "    // The cards are also the page's filter. Selection and filter are two\n",
  "    // separate crosstalk channels, and reactable intersects them per table,\n",
  "    // so a team narrows every widget while a row still highlights within it.\n",
  "    var filter = new crosstalk.FilterHandle('experience');\n",
  "    var filtering = null;\n",
  "    // The champions table is keyed by season, not by athlete, so it cannot\n",
  "    // join the crosstalk group. It takes the team by hand instead and lights\n",
  "    // its own rows; reactable re-reads meta on every render, so the highlight\n",
  "    // survives a sort or a scroll the way a stamped class would not.\n",
  "    function litChampions(team) {\n",
  "      if (window.Reactable) {\n",
  "        Reactable.setMeta('champions', { team: team || null });\n",
  "      }\n",
  "    }\n",
  "    function setFiltering(card, team) {\n",
  "      cards.forEach(function(c) { c.classList.remove('is-filtering'); });\n",
  "      if (!card) {\n",
  "        filtering = null; filter.clear(); litChampions(null); return;\n",
  "      }\n",
  "      filtering = team;\n",
  "      card.classList.add('is-filtering');\n",
  "      filter.set(rosterOf[team] || []);\n",
  "      litChampions(team);\n",
  "    }\n",
  "    cards.forEach(function(card) {\n",
  "      card.addEventListener('click', function() {\n",
  "        var team = card.getAttribute('data-team');\n",
  "        if (filtering === team) { setFiltering(null); return; }\n",
  "        // Clearing first matters: reactable intersects the two channels, so\n",
  "        // a player already selected off this team would leave every panel\n",
  "        // showing the empty overlap.\n",
  "        handle.set(null);\n",
  "        setFiltering(card, team);\n",
  "      });\n",
  "    });\n",
  "    // the Clear button lives in the navbar, where it can reach the\n",
  "    // selection but not this handle's filter; it asks for the drop instead\n",
  "    document.addEventListener('wnba:clear-filter', function() {\n",
  "      setFiltering(null);\n",
  "    });\n",
  "  });\n",
  "})();"
)
```

```{r race-prep}
# cumulative points by game date for the scoring race chart
race <- dat |>
  filter(
    season == this_year,
    game_kind == "regular",
    !is.na(athlete_display_name)
  ) |>
  select(athlete_display_name, game_date, points) |>
  mutate(game_date = as_date(game_date)) |>
  arrange(game_date) |>
  mutate(
    cum_points = cumsum(replace_na(points, 0)),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  ) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)
```

```{r efficiency-prep}
# true shooting percentage vs shot volume for the efficiency chart;
# floor of 50 field goal attempts keeps tiny-sample players out
efficiency <- dat |>
  filter(
    season == this_year,
    game_kind == "regular",
    !is.na(athlete_display_name)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    n_games = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    fga = sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  ) |>
  filter(fga >= 50) |>
  mutate(
    fga_per_game = round(fga / n_games, 1),
    ts_pct = round(100 * n_points / (2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta)), 1)
  ) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)
```

```{r experience-prep}

# named to avoid shadowing the `seasons` season-range vector defined above.
# The game_kind filter matters: this plot's y axis reads "Regular Season Games
# Played", but without it playoff and Commissioner's Cup games were counted
# too, overstating 235 careers by as much as 58 games.
experience <- dat |>
  filter(game_kind == "regular") |>
  summarise(
    n_seasons = n_distinct(season, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_games = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(athlete_display_name)
  ) |>
  arrange(n_seasons) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  drop_na(athlete)

# longest career in the data, used to size the experience plot x axis
max_seasons <- max(experience$n_seasons, na.rm = TRUE)

player_experience <- experience |>
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

points <- dat |> 
  filter(
    season == as.integer(year(now())),
    game_kind == "regular"
    ) |>
  summarise(
    n_games = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(athlete_display_name)
  ) |> 
  arrange(desc(n_games)) |> 
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |> 
  drop_na(athlete) |> 
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

```
