```{r tableoptions}
# One palette, matching the tokens in styles.scss. The dashboard used to carry
# three unrelated table skins -- orange, black and tan -- which made two tables
# side by side look like two different documents.
ink <- "#101318"
panel <- "#171a21"
panel_2 <- "#1c2029"
panel_3 <- "#232732"
line <- "#2c313c"
bone <- "#ded8cb"
mute <- "#969ea9"
wnba_orange <- "#f57b20"
# Charts only, and one chart at that: the championship stars on the Franchises
# page. The champions table beside them still lights in orange, because orange
# is what a selection means everywhere else on this page and a title is not one.
gold <- "#e8b04b"

# `wnba_black` and `wnba_tan` were kept here as aliases through the redesign
# and are gone deliberately. `wnba_black` had meant "a dark colour to draw
# against a light page", and pointing it at the page's own ink turned a
# highlighted line in the scoring race invisible. A name that means the
# opposite of what it says is worse than no name.

court_ratio <- 1/1.88

court_theme <- reactableTheme(
  color = bone,
  backgroundColor = panel,
  borderColor = line,
  stripedColor = panel_2,
  highlightColor = panel_3,
  cellPadding = "4px 6px",
  headerStyle = list(color = mute, borderColor = line),
  rowSelectedStyle = list(
    backgroundColor = panel_3,
    boxShadow = paste0("inset 3px 0 0 ", wnba_orange)
  ),
  inputStyle = list(backgroundColor = panel_2, color = bone, borderColor = line),
  selectStyle = list(backgroundColor = panel_2, color = bone),
  pageButtonHoverStyle = list(backgroundColor = panel_3),
  pageButtonActiveStyle = list(backgroundColor = panel_3, color = wnba_orange)
)

# The four charts repeated the same fifteen lines of theme. One object, added
# to each plot, so a change lands everywhere at once.
court_gg <- theme_light() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    text = element_text(color = bone),
    axis.text = element_text(color = mute),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10, color = mute),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    # ggplotly turns panel.border into a layout shape and renders its `fill =
    # NA` as opaque white, which put a white rectangle behind every chart the
    # moment the page went dark. theme_light() sets that border, and the
    # panel.background override below never reached it. An explicit transparent
    # fill keeps the frame and loses the rectangle.
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = line),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = ink, color = ink),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = ink, color = ink),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, color = bone),
    plot.margin = unit(c(16, 28, 12, 20), "points")
  )

# plotly ships one bundle covering every trace type it can draw, and at 3.6 MB
# it was the largest single thing on this page. Every chart here is a scatter,
# which the "basic" bundle draws at 1.0 MB. Every chart has to ask for it: the
# bundle is an html dependency, and one plot left on the full one embeds both.
#
# The bundle is named rather than left to `type = "auto"`, which quietly falls
# back to the full bundle when a chart needs more than basic can draw. Naming it
# stops the render and says which chart, which is the version worth being told.
basic_bundle <- function(p) partial_bundle(p, type = "basic")

# ggplotly writes one tooltip string per point, each of them repeating the column
# names -- `game_date: 2026-05-09<br />cum_points:  19<br />athlete: A'ja Wilson`.
# That is 0.58 MB of this page, and it reads like a row of a data frame rather
# than a sentence. A hovertemplate is one string for the whole trace, which
# plotly fills in from the numbers it is already holding.
#
# The athlete's name is the one thing a template cannot read off x and y, and the
# crosstalk key already carries it per point -- in plotly's order, with plotly's
# own gaps between groups -- so it is reused as customdata rather than sent a
# second time. Anything else a template needs is derived from the built trace for
# the same reason: nothing here is lined up by hand.
#
# Every axis arrives from ggplotly with hoverformat ".2f", so each field in a
# template names the format it wants.
hover <- function(p, template, custom = function(tr) tr$key) {
  p <- plotly_build(p)
  p$x$data <- lapply(p$x$data, function(tr) {
    tr$customdata <- custom(tr)
    tr$text <- NULL
    # `<extra>` is plotly's second hover box, which carries the trace name.
    # These traces have no name worth showing.
    tr$hovertemplate <- paste0(template, "<extra></extra>")
    tr
  })
  p
}

# plotly fills a template from numbers, and a number cannot pluralise the noun
# that follows it: a third of the careers in Time on the Court have played one
# season, which read as "1 seasons". Where a count can be one, the counted phrase
# is built here and travels as customdata instead. It costs 22 KB across the two
# charts it is needed on.
counted <- function(n, unit) {
  paste0(formatC(n, big.mark = ",", format = "d"), " ", unit, ifelse(n == 1, "", "s"))
}

# Handed an htmltools tag, reactable stores it as a React tag tree -- every
# element written out as `{"name":...,"attribs":...,"children":[...]}`, about
# twice the length of the markup it stands for. Handed markup with `html = TRUE`
# on the column, it stores the markup. Across this page's eighteen tables that
# is the difference between 5.8 MB and 3.2 MB.
#
# The builders still return tags, so they still cannot come out unbalanced; this
# is the hand-off, and it appears with `html = TRUE` at every site so the pair is
# always visible together.
#
# A tag tree carries no whitespace between elements, and htmltools renders one
# indented across many lines, so a plain `as.character()` would put a text node
# between every pair of elements that the page has never had. `indent = FALSE`
# drops the indents and the substitution drops the line breaks between elements
# -- only those, since a line break inside text is never both preceded by `>`
# and followed by `<`.
markup <- function(x) {
  gsub(">\n<", "><", doRenderTags(x, indent = FALSE), fixed = TRUE)
}

# The rank cell doubles as the bar: every leaderboard reads at a glance because
# the longest bar is the leader and one half as long is half the total.
bar_cell <- function(value, max_value, colour = wnba_orange) {
  width <- if (is.finite(max_value) && max_value > 0) {
    paste0(max(3, round(100 * value / max_value)), "%")
  } else {
    "0%"
  }
  div(
    style = "display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px",
    # The track takes the width the column can spare instead of the 46px it
    # used to insist on. A leaderboard that has a row to itself is a wide
    # column, and a fixed track spent that width on the gap between the name
    # and the bar rather than on the bar -- which is the thing being read.
    # Floored at what it was, and capped so a bar cannot run the width of a
    # page and stop meaning anything.
    div(
      style = paste0(
        "flex:1 1 46px;min-width:46px;max-width:320px;",
        "height:8px;background:", panel_3, ";border-radius:2px"
      ),
      div(style = paste0(
        "width:", width, ";height:100%;background:", colour, ";border-radius:2px"
      ))
    ),
    span(style = "font-weight:600", format(value, big.mark = ","))
  )
}

# Sixteen near-identical thirty-line chunks collapsed to one call each. The
# eight leaderboards on a page are now eight tabs of a single card rather than
# eight cards spread over two rows, which is where the height for the player
# panels came from.
stat_card <- function(df, col, label) {
  top <- max(df[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)

  # `stat()` returns a `total_seasons` column for the career frames and omits it
  # for the single-season ones, and reactable rejects a colDef naming a column
  # that is not there. Build the list from what the frame actually has.
  cols <- list(
    rank = colDef(name = "#", maxWidth = sm, style = list(color = mute)),
    # Capped, or the name column takes every pixel a wide row has spare and
    # opens a hand's width between a player and her own bar.
    athlete = colDef(name = "Athlete", minWidth = 130, maxWidth = 260),
    # Wide enough for "Golden State Valkyries" on one line: a team column that
    # wraps stands every row it appears in two lines tall, which is what the
    # all-time table beside it does. Muted, because the subject of a row here
    # is the player and the number, and the club is the context around them.
    latest_team = colDef(
      name = "Team", minWidth = 170, maxWidth = 200, style = list(color = mute)
    ),
    # The school she came up at, muted for the same reason the club is: the
    # subject of a row here is the player and the number. Blank rather than a
    # dash where there is none, because a fifth of this league came up through
    # European, Australian and Asian clubs and never attended one -- a dash in
    # a column of school names reads as a missing value rather than as a career
    # that took another route.
    college = colDef(
      name = "College",
      minWidth = 130,
      maxWidth = 180,
      style = list(color = mute),
      na = ""
    ),
    total_seasons = colDef(name = "Seasons", maxWidth = md),
    seasons = colDef(name = "Span", maxWidth = lg, style = list(color = mute))
  )
  cols <- cols[intersect(names(cols), names(df))]
  cols[[col]] <- colDef(
    name = label,
    minWidth = 140,
    html = TRUE,
    # A bar column is read from its left edge, where every bar starts, so the
    # header belongs there too. Reactable right-aligns a numeric column by
    # default, which put the word at the far end of a run of bars that all
    # begin at the near one. `align` moves only the header here: the cell holds
    # a full-width flex row, which text alignment cannot shift.
    align = "left",
    cell = function(value) markup(bar_cell(value, top))
  )

  # Named the way the comparison table names the same quantity -- "Assists /
  # Game" -- so one phrase means one thing across the page. `fmt1` rather than
  # a formatted string in the frame, so the column still sorts as a number.
  if ("per_game" %in% names(df)) {
    cols$per_game <- colDef(
      name = paste0(label, " / Game"),
      maxWidth = 130,
      align = "right",
      cell = function(value) fmt1(value)
    )
  }

  df |>
    SharedData$new(key = ~athlete, group = "experience") |>
    reactable(
      compact = TRUE,
      highlight = TRUE,
      striped = TRUE,
      filterable = FALSE,
      defaultPageSize = 15,
      defaultSorted = list(rank = "asc"),
      theme = court_theme,
      columns = cols
    )
}
```

```{r alltime-prep}
# The four charts that sit beside Time on the Court. The two keyed by athlete
# answer the crosstalk selection; the two that describe the league cannot, and
# are drawn straight rather than through ggplotly for it.

# --- The Chase: every career's running total ------------------------------
# One mark per season rather than per game. At game resolution these 178
# careers are 56,000 marks in a page that already weighs 13 MB, and a running
# total is smooth enough that a season's resolution draws the same curve.
career_seasons <- dat |>
  filter(game_kind == "regular", !is.na(athlete_display_name)) |>
  summarise(
    season_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    season_games = n_distinct(game_id),
    .by = c(athlete_display_name, season)
  ) |>
  arrange(athlete_display_name, season) |>
  mutate(
    total_points = cumsum(season_points),
    career_games = cumsum(season_games),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  )

# 1,500 career points is the line between the pack and the crowd: 178 careers,
# enough that most players worth selecting have a curve to light up, few enough
# that the curves stay separable.
chase <- career_seasons |>
  filter(max(total_points) >= 1500, .by = athlete_display_name) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

# --- Efficiency over a whole career ---------------------------------------
# The season chart's twin, with the floor raised from 50 attempts to 500: over
# 22 years a 50-attempt career is a cup of coffee, not a shooting record.
career_efficiency <- dat |>
  filter(game_kind == "regular", !is.na(athlete_display_name)) |>
  summarise(
    n_games = n_distinct(game_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    fga = sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = athlete_display_name
  ) |>
  filter(fga >= 500) |>
  mutate(
    fga_per_game = round(fga / n_games, 1),
    ts_pct = round(100 * n_points / (2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta)), 1)
  ) |>
  rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
  SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

# --- What the league does with the ball ------------------------------------
# Per team-game, so expansion and a lengthening schedule cannot masquerade as a
# change in how the game is played.
league_season <- dat |>
  filter(game_kind == "regular") |>
  summarise(
    team_games = n_distinct(paste(game_id, team_id)),
    threes = sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    scored = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = season
  ) |>
  transmute(
    season,
    `Threes attempted` = threes / team_games,
    `Points scored` = scored / team_games
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-season, names_to = "measure", values_to = "per_game") |>
  # threes first: it is the panel the chart is named for
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("Threes attempted", "Points scored")))

# --- Attendance ------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsed on every render since the schedule was first loaded, and shown
# nowhere until now. ESPN did not record it before 2013: a handful of games in
# 2007, 2011 and 2012 carry a figure, and averaging a season off three games
# would invent a number. So a season has to have counted half its games to be
# drawn at all, which starts the series at 2013 and drops 2020 -- that one for
# the honest reason, a season played in a bubble with nobody in the seats.
attendance <- sched |>
  filter(game_kind == "regular", status_type_completed %in% TRUE) |>
  mutate(attendance = as.integer(attendance)) |>
  summarise(
    counted = sum(attendance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    coverage = mean(attendance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    per_game = mean(attendance[attendance > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = season
  ) |>
  filter(coverage >= 0.5) |>
  # 2020 back as a hole rather than as a missing row, so the line breaks there
  # instead of stepping over it as though nothing happened
  complete(season = full_seq(season, 1)) |>
  arrange(season)
```

```{r franchise-prep}
# Every franchise the league has had, and every name each one played under.
# This is the only table on the dashboard typed out by hand, and it is typed
# out because half of it is older than the evidence: the box scores start in
# 2004, and Cleveland, Miami, the first Portland, and the moves out of Utah and
# Orlando had all happened by then. The part the box scores *can* see is checked
# against them below, so what is taken on trust is only ever the part before
# 2004 -- and a franchise that quietly changed name since would fail the render
# rather than sit here wrong.
franchise_eras <- tribble(
  ~lineage,    ~era,                       ~from, ~to,
  "liberty",   "New York Liberty",          1997, NA,
  "sparks",    "Los Angeles Sparks",        1997, NA,
  "mercury",   "Phoenix Mercury",           1997, NA,
  "aces",      "Utah Starzz",               1997, 2002,
  "aces",      "San Antonio Silver Stars",  2003, 2013,
  "aces",      "San Antonio Stars",         2014, 2017,
  "aces",      "Las Vegas Aces",            2018, NA,
  "sting",     "Charlotte Sting",           1997, 2006,
  "rockers",   "Cleveland Rockers",         1997, 2003,
  "comets",    "Houston Comets",            1997, 2008,
  "monarchs",  "Sacramento Monarchs",       1997, 2009,
  "wings",     "Detroit Shock",             1998, 2009,
  "wings",     "Tulsa Shock",               2010, 2015,
  "wings",     "Dallas Wings",              2016, NA,
  "mystics",   "Washington Mystics",        1998, NA,
  "lynx",      "Minnesota Lynx",            1999, NA,
  "sun",       "Orlando Miracle",           1999, 2002,
  "sun",       "Connecticut Sun",           2003, NA,
  "fever",     "Indiana Fever",             2000, NA,
  "storm",     "Seattle Storm",             2000, NA,
  "sol",       "Miami Sol",                 2000, 2002,
  # two unrelated franchises, twenty-four years apart, under one name: ESPN
  # issues the 2026 team its own id rather than the folded one's, so even the
  # source treats them as strangers
  "fire-i",    "Portland Fire",             2000, 2002,
  "sky",       "Chicago Sky",               2006, NA,
  "dream",     "Atlanta Dream",             2008, NA,
  "valkyries", "Golden State Valkyries",    2025, NA,
  "tempo",     "Toronto Tempo",             2026, NA,
  "fire-ii",   "Portland Fire",             2026, NA
)

first_season <- min(dat$season)
last_season <- max(dat$season)

# The gate. Every era that overlaps the box scores has to appear in them under
# exactly that name for exactly those seasons, and every name in them has to be
# an era here -- so a new franchise, or a rename, cannot slip past unrecorded.
era_check <- franchise_eras |>
  mutate(end = coalesce(to, last_season)) |>
  filter(end >= first_season) |>
  mutate(
    expect_from = pmax(from, first_season),
    expect_to = pmin(end, last_season)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    summarise(dat, seen_from = min(season), seen_to = max(season),
              .by = team_display_name),
    by = c("era" = "team_display_name")
  )

stopifnot(
  "franchise_eras disagrees with the box scores" =
    isTRUE(all.equal(era_check$expect_from, era_check$seen_from)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(era_check$expect_to, era_check$seen_to)),
  "a team in the box scores has no era in franchise_eras" =
    length(setdiff(unique(dat$team_display_name), franchise_eras$era)) == 0
)

# One franchise, one colour, carried across every name it has answered to --
# which is what says the four Aces bars are one club and not four. The colour is
# the one it wears now, so a franchise that has folded has none: those go grey,
# and the greying is the chart's way of saying the story ended.
team_hue <- dat |>
  arrange(game_date) |>
  summarise(colour = accent(last(team_color)), .by = team_display_name)

franchises <- franchise_eras |>
  mutate(
    end = coalesce(to, last_season),
    active = any(is.na(to)),
    current = era[which.max(from)],
    debut = min(from),
    .by = lineage
  ) |>
  left_join(team_hue, by = c("current" = "team_display_name")) |>
  mutate(colour = if_else(active, colour, mute))

# oldest at the top, and within an arrival year the clubs still playing before
# the ones that are not, so the page reads down through the league's growth
franchise_rows <- franchises |>
  distinct(lineage, debut, active, current) |>
  arrange(desc(debut), active, desc(current)) |>
  mutate(row = row_number())

# The chart's own page, so it is drawn at the size of one. These three sit
# together because the label rule below is worked out from all of them.
lineage_fig_w <- 13
lineage_fig_h <- 8
# Thin lines leave room the thick bars did not, so the names are set larger.
lineage_size <- 3.7

# How wide one character is, in seasons -- the unit the eras are measured in.
# A character of type averages a little over half its point size across, and
# `.pt` is ggplot's own conversion from a text size to points.
lineage_span <- (last_season + 0.35) - (min(franchise_eras$from) - 0.35)
char_seasons <- (0.58 * lineage_size * .pt / 72) /
  ((lineage_fig_w - 0.9) / lineage_span)

franchises <- franchises |>
  left_join(select(franchise_rows, lineage, row), by = "lineage") |>
  # Labels sit at the left end of their era and read rightward, which works
  # only while the era is longer than the name: "San Antonio Stars" is four
  # seasons wide and ran into "Las Vegas Aces" beside it. So measure both in
  # the same units -- seasons -- and let a name that outgrows its era hang off
  # the era's right end instead, back over ground the line has already covered.
  # Eras still running have no room to their right at all and do the same.
  #
  # The width of a name is worked out from the chart's own geometry rather than
  # measured off a screenshot, so that resizing the figure or the label moves
  # this with it instead of silently invalidating it.
  mutate(
    bar_seasons = end - from + 0.4,
    name_seasons = nchar(era) * char_seasons,
    from_right = (name_seasons > bar_seasons & from != max(from)) |
      from >= last_season - 3,
    .by = lineage
  )

# A dot where each era finished, and nothing where it began: a line that starts
# bare and ends on a dot reads in the direction the seasons run, and the start
# is already marked by the line itself leaving the empty ground to its left.
# The right-hand end of an era still being played is the exception -- 2026 is
# where the record stops rather than where the franchise did, so that end
# carries the club's crest, the one mark that says who is still out there.
era_ends <- franchises |>
  select(era, row, colour, to, end) |>
  mutate(still_running = is.na(to))

# ESPN serves the crests from a CDN, and this chart is a static image, so they
# have to be on disk by the time it is drawn. Fetch each one once and keep it:
# a render with no network then costs nothing, and the first render costs
# fifteen small files. Anything that fails to arrive simply keeps its dot, so
# an offline first render draws the chart it always drew rather than no chart.
logo_dir <- "logos"
if (!dir.exists(logo_dir)) dir.create(logo_dir)

logo_url <- dat |>
  arrange(game_date) |>
  summarise(url = last(team_logo), .by = team_display_name)

crests <- franchises |>
  filter(is.na(to)) |>
  select(era, row, end) |>
  left_join(logo_url, by = c("era" = "team_display_name")) |>
  mutate(
    file = file.path(logo_dir, paste0(str_replace_all(tolower(era), "[^a-z]+", "-"), ".png")),
    image = map2(espn_img(url, 96), file, function(src, dest) {
      if (!file.exists(dest)) {
        try(curl::curl_download(src, dest), silent = TRUE)
      }
      if (file.exists(dest)) {
        try(as.raster(png::readPNG(dest)), silent = TRUE)
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    })
  ) |>
  filter(map_lgl(image, \(x) inherits(x, "raster")))

# A crest has to come out square, and the two axes are in different units, so
# its width in seasons is its height in rows converted through the panel's own
# proportions. The 1.2 and 1.5 are the room the title, subtitle and axis take
# out of the figure; they only have to be close.
crest_rows <- 0.86
row_in <- (lineage_fig_h - 1.5) / (nrow(franchise_rows) + 1.4)
season_in <- (lineage_fig_w - 1.2) / lineage_span
crest_seasons <- crest_rows * row_in / season_in

franchises <- franchises |>
  mutate(
    # a right-hand label has to clear the crest now standing at that end
    label_x = case_when(
      !from_right ~ from - 0.2,
      is.na(to) ~ end - crest_seasons / 2 - 0.2,
      .default = end + 0.2
    )
  )

# Three kinds of end, not two: an era that finished, an era still being played
# whose crest arrived, and an era still being played whose crest did not. The
# last keeps the hollow dot, so a failed download costs a crest and not a mark.
era_ends <- era_ends |>
  mutate(
    mark = case_when(
      !still_running ~ "closed",
      era %in% crests$era ~ "crest",
      .default = "open"
    )
  )

# Every title, on the line of the club that won it. `champions` carries the name
# a club won under and `franchise_eras` the name it played under, so the two
# meet on the name and the season decides which era of that name it was.
titles <- champions |>
  inner_join(
    select(franchises, era, row, from, end),
    by = join_by(champion == era)
  ) |>
  filter(season >= from, season <= end)

# The second gate on this chunk, and the one the seven hand-typed titles rest
# on. A championship that lands on no era, or on two, is a name spelled wrong
# here or a rename ESPN has made since -- either way something this chart would
# have drawn in the wrong place.
stopifnot(
  "a title does not land on exactly one franchise era" =
    nrow(titles) == nrow(champions)
)

# A five-pointed star per title, standing on the line at the season it was won.
# R has no filled five-pointed plotting symbol -- pch 8 is an asterisk -- so it
# is drawn as ten vertices at alternating radii, the inner one the pentagram's
# own 1/phi^2. `star_rows` is the outer radius, about half a crest; the two axes
# are in different units, so its width in seasons comes from the same conversion
# the crests take above.
#
# A title in the season the record stops lands where the crest stands, and the
# crest would cover it. That star moves left along the line to sit against the
# crest, because hiding the crest or the title both lose the point of the mark.
star_rows <- 0.22
star_seasons <- star_rows * row_in / season_in

star_points <- tibble(
  angle = seq(pi / 2, pi / 2 + 2 * pi, length.out = 11)[-11],
  radius = rep(c(1, 0.382), length.out = 10)
)

stars <- titles |>
  mutate(
    title_id = row_number(),
    star_x = if_else(
      season == last_season & champion %in% crests$era,
      season - crest_seasons / 2 - star_seasons,
      season
    )
  ) |>
  cross_join(star_points) |>
  mutate(
    x = star_x + star_seasons * radius * cos(angle),
    y = row + star_rows * radius * sin(angle)
  )
```

```{r playoffs-2026-prep}
playoff_year <- 2026L

# The year stays fixed when the current-season page moves on. The published
# bracket settles the two tied seeds as well as the four first-round pairings:
# https://www.wnba.com/playoffs/2026
official_seed_names <- c(
  "Minnesota Lynx", "Golden State Valkyries", "Las Vegas Aces",
  "Atlanta Dream", "Washington Mystics", "Indiana Fever",
  "Dallas Wings", "New York Liberty"
)

regular_2026 <- dat |>
  filter(season == playoff_year, game_kind == "regular")

regular_2026_schedule <- sched |>
  filter(
    season == playoff_year, game_kind == "regular",
    status_type_name != "STATUS_POSTPONED"
  )

regular_team_games <- regular_2026 |>
  distinct(game_id, team_id, team_display_name, team_abbreviation,
           team_logo, team_color, team_winner)

regular_team_records <- regular_team_games |>
  summarise(
    name = last(team_display_name),
    abbreviation = last(team_abbreviation),
    logo = espn_img(last(team_logo), 52),
    color = accent(last(team_color)),
    games = n_distinct(game_id),
    w = sum(team_winner %in% TRUE),
    l = sum(team_winner %in% FALSE),
    .by = team_id
  )

stopifnot(
  "2026 regular season does not have 330 played games" =
    n_distinct(regular_2026$game_id) == 330L,
  "2026 regular schedule does not match its box scores" =
    setequal(regular_2026_schedule$game_id, regular_2026$game_id),
  "a 2026 team does not have 44 regular-season games" =
    nrow(regular_team_records) == 15L && all(regular_team_records$games == 44L),
  "the official 2026 seeds do not match the top eight records" =
    setequal(official_seed_names, regular_team_records |>
      arrange(desc(w), desc(w / (w + l))) |>
      slice_head(n = 8) |>
      pull(name)),
  "the official 2026 seed order does not match the standings" =
    this_year != playoff_year ||
      identical(head(standings$name, 8L), official_seed_names)
)

playoff_seeds <- regular_team_records |>
  filter(name %in% official_seed_names) |>
  mutate(seed = match(name, official_seed_names)) |>
  arrange(seed)

# The schedule has generic future slots. Headlines identify the round even
# when ESPN's type_id does not: 2026 semifinal slots have type_id 1.
post_box <- dat |>
  filter(season == playoff_year, game_kind == "post")

post_team_scores <- post_box |>
  distinct(game_id, home_away, team_id, team_score, team_display_name)

stopifnot(
  "a playoff team has conflicting box scores" =
    all((post_team_scores |> count(game_id, home_away))$n == 1L)
)

complete_post_team_scores <- post_team_scores |>
  filter(home_away %in% c("home", "away")) |>
  group_by(game_id) |>
  filter(n_distinct(team_id) == 2L, n_distinct(home_away) == 2L,
         all(!is.na(team_score))) |>
  ungroup()

post_scores <- if (nrow(complete_post_team_scores) == 0L) {
  tibble(
    game_id = integer(), box_home_id = integer(), box_away_id = integer(),
    home_points = integer(), away_points = integer(),
    box_home_name = character(), box_away_name = character()
  )
} else {
  complete_post_team_scores |>
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols = game_id, names_from = home_away,
      values_from = c(team_id, team_score, team_display_name),
      names_glue = "{home_away}_{.value}"
    ) |>
    transmute(
      game_id,
      box_home_id = as.integer(home_team_id),
      box_away_id = as.integer(away_team_id),
      home_points = home_team_score,
      away_points = away_team_score,
      box_home_name = home_team_display_name,
      box_away_name = away_team_display_name
    )
}

post_schedule <- sched |>
  filter(season == playoff_year, game_kind == "post") |>
  mutate(
    round = case_when(
      str_detect(notes_headline, regex("First Round", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "First Round",
      str_detect(notes_headline, regex("Semifinals", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Semifinals",
      str_detect(notes_headline, regex("WNBA Finals", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Finals",
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    game_number = as.integer(str_match(notes_headline, "Game ([1-7])")[, 2]),
    conditional = str_detect(notes_headline, regex("If Necessary", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    home_id = as.integer(home_id),
    away_id = as.integer(away_id)
  ) |>
  left_join(post_scores, by = "game_id") |>
  mutate(
    home_id = coalesce(box_home_id, home_id),
    away_id = coalesce(box_away_id, away_id),
    home_display_name = coalesce(box_home_name, home_display_name),
    away_display_name = coalesce(box_away_name, away_display_name),
    completed = !is.na(home_points) & !is.na(away_points) &
      home_points != away_points,
    winner_id = if_else(
      completed,
      if_else(home_points > away_points, home_id, away_id),
      NA_integer_
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  "unrecognized 2026 playoff round or game number" =
    !anyNA(post_schedule$round) && !anyNA(post_schedule$game_number),
  "2026 playoff schedule has duplicate game IDs" =
    !anyDuplicated(post_schedule$game_id),
  "a reported final is missing a complete box score" =
    all(!(post_schedule$status_type_completed %in% TRUE) | post_schedule$completed)
)

post_team_records <- if (any(post_schedule$completed)) {
  bind_rows(
    post_schedule |>
      filter(completed) |>
      transmute(team_id = home_id, scored = home_points, allowed = away_points,
                won = winner_id == home_id),
    post_schedule |>
      filter(completed) |>
      transmute(team_id = away_id, scored = away_points, allowed = home_points,
                won = winner_id == away_id)
  ) |>
    summarise(
      w = sum(won), l = sum(!won),
      pf = mean(scored), pa = mean(allowed), .by = team_id
    )
} else {
  tibble(team_id = integer(), w = integer(), l = integer(),
         pf = double(), pa = double())
}

# A series is defined by its round and its two team IDs. Future TBD slots
# cannot be assigned to one, even though their date and broadcaster are known.
series_state <- function(id, series_round, a_id, b_id, wins_needed) {
  if (is.na(a_id) || is.na(b_id)) {
    return(tibble(
      series_id = id, round = series_round, a_id = a_id, b_id = b_id,
      a_wins = 0L, b_wins = 0L, wins_needed = wins_needed,
      winner_id = NA_integer_
    ))
  }
  games <- post_schedule |>
    filter(
      .data$round == series_round, completed,
      (home_id == a_id & away_id == b_id) |
        (home_id == b_id & away_id == a_id)
    )
  a_wins <- sum(games$winner_id == a_id)
  b_wins <- sum(games$winner_id == b_id)
  tibble(
    series_id = id, round = series_round, a_id = a_id, b_id = b_id,
    a_wins = a_wins, b_wins = b_wins, wins_needed = wins_needed,
    winner_id = if (a_wins >= wins_needed) a_id else if (b_wins >= wins_needed) b_id else NA_integer_
  )
}

seed_id <- playoff_seeds$team_id
first_round <- bind_rows(
  series_state(1L, "First Round", seed_id[1], seed_id[8], 2L),
  series_state(2L, "First Round", seed_id[4], seed_id[5], 2L),
  series_state(3L, "First Round", seed_id[2], seed_id[7], 2L),
  series_state(4L, "First Round", seed_id[3], seed_id[6], 2L)
)
semifinals <- bind_rows(
  series_state(5L, "Semifinals", first_round$winner_id[1], first_round$winner_id[2], 3L),
  series_state(6L, "Semifinals", first_round$winner_id[3], first_round$winner_id[4], 3L)
)
final_series <- series_state(
  7L, "Finals", semifinals$winner_id[1], semifinals$winner_id[2], 4L
)
playoff_series <- bind_rows(first_round, semifinals, final_series)

pair_key <- function(a, b) {
  ifelse(is.na(a) | is.na(b) | a < 0 | b < 0,
         NA_character_, paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b), sep = ":"))
}

playoff_series <- playoff_series |>
  mutate(pair = pair_key(a_id, b_id))
round_status <- playoff_series |>
  summarise(round_decided = all(!is.na(winner_id)), .by = round)
post_schedule <- post_schedule |>
  mutate(pair = pair_key(home_id, away_id)) |>
  left_join(
    playoff_series |>
      select(round, pair, series_id, series_winner = winner_id),
    by = c("round", "pair"), na_matches = "never"
  ) |>
  left_join(round_status, by = "round")

stopifnot(
  "a played playoff game has no bracket series" =
    all(!post_schedule$completed | !is.na(post_schedule$series_id))
)

# ESPN's schedule names one outlet. The league also names simulcasts for
# particular 2026 slots: https://www.wnba.com/news/2026-wnba-postseason-faq
watch_options <- function(outlet, round) {
  case_when(
    is.na(outlet) | outlet == "" ~ "Broadcast not listed",
    outlet == "NBC" & round %in% c("Semifinals", "Finals") ~ "NBC / Peacock",
    outlet == "Peacock" & round == "Semifinals" ~ "Peacock / NBCSN",
    outlet == "USA Net" & round == "Finals" ~ "USA Network / Peacock",
    outlet == "USA Net" ~ "USA Network",
    TRUE ~ outlet
  )
}

playoff_schedule <- post_schedule |>
  filter(!(conditional & !completed &
             (!is.na(series_winner) | round_decided))) |>
  mutate(
    time_tbd = is.na(game_date_time) | hour(game_date_time) == 0L,
    when = paste0(
      format(game_date, "%a, %b "), as.integer(format(game_date, "%d")),
      " · ", if_else(
        time_tbd, "Time TBD",
        paste0(format(game_date_time, "%I:%M %p",
                      tz = "America/New_York"), " ET")
      )
    ),
    matchup = if_else(
      home_id > 0 & away_id > 0 &
        home_display_name != "TBD" & away_display_name != "TBD",
      paste0(away_display_name, " at ", home_display_name),
      "Teams TBD"
    ),
    market = if_else(
      is.na(broadcast_market) | broadcast_market == "national",
      "", paste0(" · ", broadcast_market, " market")
    ),
    watch = paste0(watch_options(broadcast_name, round), market),
    game = paste0("Game ", game_number, if_else(conditional, " if necessary", "")),
    result = if_else(
      completed,
      paste0(away_points, "–", home_points, " final"),
      "Scheduled"
    ),
    series = if_else(
      is.na(series_id), "Pairing pending", paste0("Series ", series_id)
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(game_date, time_tbd, game_date_time, game_id) |>
  # `day` numbers the dates that have a game, 1 for the earliest. The date
  # slider above the schedule table steps through these rather than through the
  # calendar, so every stop on it removes at least one game and none is a rest
  # day. A number, because reactable serialises a Date column as a string.
  mutate(
    day = dense_rank(game_date),
    day_label = paste0(format(game_date, "%a, %b "),
                       as.integer(format(game_date, "%d"))),
    date_class = paste0("ps-date-", (day - 1L) %% 3L + 1L)
  ) |>
  select(when, matchup, watch, market, round, series, game, result,
         game_id, completed, day, day_label, date_class)

playoff_days <- playoff_schedule |> distinct(day, day_label) |> arrange(day)
```

```{r playoffs-2026-players}
post_has_games <- nrow(post_box) > 0L
playoff_empty <- function() {
  div(class = "playoff-empty", "No playoff games completed in the current data.")
}

if (post_has_games) {
  pdat_post <- player_stats(post_box, season_part = "post", my_season = playoff_year) |>
    left_join(player_college, by = join_by(athlete))

  post_doubles <- post_box |>
    transmute(
      athlete = athlete_display_name,
      game_id,
      double_count = rowSums(cbind(
        points >= 10, rebounds >= 10, assists >= 10,
        steals >= 10, blocks >= 10
      ), na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
    summarise(
      double_double = sum(double_count >= 2),
      triple_double = sum(double_count >= 3),
      .by = athlete
    )

  post_players <- pdat_post |>
    left_join(post_doubles, by = "athlete") |>
    mutate(
      points_per_game = total_points / total_games,
      rank = min_rank(desc(total_points))
    ) |>
    arrange(rank, athlete) |>
    select(rank, athlete, total_points, total_games, points_per_game,
           double_double, triple_double, position, latest_team, everything())
  post_players_df <- post_players
  post_players <- SharedData$new(post_players_df, group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

  post_game_log <- post_box |>
    left_join(post_schedule |> select(game_id, round), by = "game_id") |>
    arrange(athlete_display_name, game_date, game_id) |>
    transmute(
      athlete = athlete_display_name,
      d = short_date(game_date), round,
      opp = opponent_team_abbreviation,
      p = as.integer(points),
      won = team_winner %in% TRUE
    ) |>
    nest(log = c(d, round, opp, p, won))

  post_profile <- post_box |>
    summarise(
      shot = espn_img(first(na.omit(athlete_headshot_href)), 220),
      logo = espn_img(team_logo[which.max(game_date)], 52),
      color = accent(team_color[which.max(game_date)]),
      team = team_display_name[which.max(game_date)],
      pos = first(na.omit(athlete_position_abbreviation)),
      jersey = first(na.omit(athlete_jersey)),
      g = n_distinct(game_id),
      mins = sum(minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
      pts = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
      reb = sum(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE),
      ast = sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE),
      stl = sum(steals, na.rm = TRUE),
      blk = sum(blocks, na.rm = TRUE),
      fgm = sum(field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      fga = sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
      tpm = sum(three_point_field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      tpa = sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
      ftm = sum(free_throws_made, na.rm = TRUE),
      fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
    mutate(
      mpg = mins / g, ppg = pts / g, rpg = reb / g,
      apg = ast / g, spg = stl / g, bpg = blk / g,
      fgp = pct_of(fgm, fga), tpp = pct_of(tpm, tpa),
      ftp = pct_of(ftm, fta),
      ts = pct_of(pts, 2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta))
    ) |>
    left_join(post_game_log, by = "athlete")
  post_profile_by <- split(post_profile, post_profile$athlete)

  post_compare_raw <- post_box |>
    summarise(
      headshot = espn_img(first(na.omit(athlete_headshot_href)), 120),
      team = team_name[which.max(game_date)],
      games = n_distinct(game_id),
      total_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
      ppg = total_points / games,
      apg = sum(assists, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
      rpg = sum(rebounds, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
      spg = sum(steals, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
      bpg = sum(blocks, na.rm = TRUE) / games,
      fg_pct = pct_of(sum(field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
                      sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE)),
      tp_pct = pct_of(sum(three_point_field_goals_made, na.rm = TRUE),
                      sum(three_point_field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE)),
      ft_pct = pct_of(sum(free_throws_made, na.rm = TRUE),
                      sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(total_points), athlete_display_name)

  post_compare_wide <- post_compare_raw |>
    transmute(
      athlete = athlete_display_name,
      Photo = photo_cell(headshot, team),
      `Games Played` = as.character(games),
      `Total Points` = as.character(total_points),
      `Points / Game` = fmt1(ppg),
      `Assists / Game` = fmt1(apg),
      `Rebounds / Game` = fmt1(rpg),
      `Steals / Game` = fmt1(spg),
      `Blocks / Game` = fmt1(bpg),
      `FG%` = fmt_pct(fg_pct),
      `3P%` = fmt_pct(tp_pct),
      `FT%` = fmt_pct(ft_pct)
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(-athlete, names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(stat = if_else(stat == "Photo", "", stat)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = athlete, values_from = value)
  post_compare_players <- setdiff(names(post_compare_wide), "stat")
  post_compare_default <- head(post_compare_raw$athlete_display_name, 8)

  post_compare_js <- paste0(
    "(function() {\n",
    "  var players = ", jsonlite::toJSON(post_compare_players), ";\n",
    "  var defaults = ", jsonlite::toJSON(post_compare_default), ";\n",
    "  window.addEventListener('load', function() {\n",
    "    var selection = new crosstalk.SelectionHandle('experience');\n",
    "    var filter = new crosstalk.FilterHandle('experience');\n",
    "    function apply() {\n",
    "      var chosen = selection.value;\n",
    "      var filtered = filter.filteredKeys;\n",
    "      var shown = chosen && chosen.length ? chosen :\n",
    "        filtered && filtered.length ? filtered : defaults;\n",
    "      var hidden = players.filter(function(p) { return shown.indexOf(p) < 0; });\n",
    "      if (window.Reactable) Reactable.setHiddenColumns('post-compare-table', hidden);\n",
    "    }\n",
    "    selection.on('change', apply);\n",
    "    filter.on('change', apply);\n",
    "    apply();\n",
    "  });\n",
    "})();"
  )

  post_race <- post_box |>
    arrange(game_date, game_id) |>
    mutate(
      cum_points = cumsum(points),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    transmute(athlete = athlete_display_name,
              game_date = as_date(game_date), cum_points) |>
    SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

  post_points <- post_box |>
    summarise(
      n_games = n_distinct(game_id),
      n_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    rename(athlete = athlete_display_name) |>
    SharedData$new(group = "experience", key = ~athlete)

  post_efficiency_df <- post_box |>
    summarise(
      n_games = n_distinct(game_id),
      fga = sum(field_goals_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
      fta = sum(free_throws_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_points = sum(points, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = athlete_display_name
    ) |>
    filter(fga >= 20) |>
    mutate(
      fga_per_game = round(fga / n_games, 1),
      ts_pct = pct_of(n_points, 2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta))
    ) |>
    rename(athlete = athlete_display_name)
  if (nrow(post_efficiency_df) > 0L) {
    post_efficiency <- SharedData$new(
      post_efficiency_df, group = "experience", key = ~athlete
    )
  }

  stat_post_dfs <- stat_names |>
    set_names() |>
    map(\(name) stat(pdat_post, col = {{ name }}))
}

post_crest_cell <- function(name) {
  p <- post_profile_by[[name]]
  logo <- if (is.null(p) || is.na(p$logo)) NULL else {
    tags$img(src = p$logo, alt = "", width = 18, height = 18,
             loading = "lazy", style = "object-fit:contain")
  }
  div(class = "playoff-athlete", logo, span(name))
}

post_dossier <- function(name) {
  p <- post_profile_by[[name]]
  if (is.null(p)) return(playoff_empty())
  gl <- p$log[[1]]
  top <- max(gl$p, 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  bars <- pmap(
    list(gl$p, gl$won, gl$d, gl$round, gl$opp),
    \(points_, won_, date_, round_, opp_) div(
      class = "dsr-bar",
      style = paste0("height:", max(round(100 * points_ / top), 3), "%"),
      title = paste0(date_, " · ", round_, " vs ", opp_, ": ",
                     points_, " pts (", if (won_) "W" else "L", ")")
    )
  )
  div(
    class = "dossier", style = paste0("--team:", p$color),
    div(class = "dsr-id",
        if (is.na(p$shot)) NULL else
          tags$img(class = "dsr-shot", src = p$shot, alt = "", loading = "lazy"),
        div(class = "dsr-name", name),
        div(class = "dsr-meta", paste(c(
          if (!is.na(p$jersey)) paste0("#", p$jersey), p$pos, p$team
        ), collapse = " · "))),
    div(class = "dsr-body",
        div(class = "dsr-grid",
            stat_cell("Games", p$g),
            stat_cell("Min/G", fmt1(p$mpg)),
            stat_cell("Pts/G", fmt1(p$ppg), lead = TRUE),
            stat_cell("Reb/G", fmt1(p$rpg)),
            stat_cell("Ast/G", fmt1(p$apg)),
            stat_cell("Stl/G", fmt1(p$spg)),
            stat_cell("Blk/G", fmt1(p$bpg)),
            stat_cell("FG%", fmt_pct(p$fgp)),
            stat_cell("3P%", fmt_pct(p$tpp)),
            stat_cell("FT%", fmt_pct(p$ftp)),
            stat_cell("TS%", fmt_pct(p$ts))),
        div(class = "dsr-logtitle", "Points in each playoff game. Hover for the date, round, opponent, and result."),
        div(class = "dsr-log", bars))
  )
}
```

```{r teamcards}
#| title: "Click a team to filter the dashboard"

# bslib walks this tag tree and stamps `html-fill-item html-fill-container` on
# every node, which turns each card and the row inside it into a column
# flexbox. The stylesheet answers that by scoping these rules under #standings,
# which outranks a single class; emitting the markup as text instead only
# traded the problem for pandoc reading htmltools' indentation as a code block.
div(
  id = "standings",
  pmap(
    standings,
    function(team_abbreviation, name, city, color, logo, w, l, pf, pa, form) {
      div(
        class = "tcard",
        # the selection script matches this against the main table's
        # latest_team; both are last(team_display_name)
        `data-team` = name,
        # One line, so the club's full name and what it scores and allows have
        # nowhere to sit on the card and sit on the card instead. "for and
        # against" left it unsaid whether these were season totals or averages;
        # verbs carry the rate that the nouns did not.
        title = sprintf(
          "%s \u00b7 scores %.0f \u00b7 allows %.0f a game", name, pf, pa
        ),
        style = paste0("--team:", color),
        div(
          class = "tc-top",
          if (is.na(logo)) NULL else tags$img(src = logo, alt = "", loading = "lazy"),
          span(class = "tc-name", city),
          span(class = "tc-rec", paste0(w, "\u2013", l)),
          span(class = "tc-form", map(form, \(r) tags$i(class = r)))
        )
      )
    }
  )
)
```

```{r race}
#| title: Scoring Race
race_plot <- race |>
  ggplot(aes(x = game_date, y = cum_points, group = athlete)) +
  geom_line(
    color = wnba_orange,
    linewidth = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Cumulative Points this Regular Season",
    subtitle = "each line is a player - select players in the tables",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Points Scored"
  ) +
  court_gg

ggplotly(
  race_plot,
  tooltip = c("athlete", "game_date", "cum_points")
) |>
  # White and thick. This used to highlight in `wnba_black`, which worked
  # against a light page and now names the page's own ink -- a selected line
  # was being drawn near-black on a near-black panel and disappeared.
  highlight(
    color = "#ffffff",
    opacityDim = 0.35,
    selected = attrs_selected(line = list(width = 3.5))
  ) |>
  basic_bundle() |>
  # the only chart whose template needs a second field: ggplotly renders a date
  # scale as a plain numeric axis carrying day numbers, so `%{x}` would read
  # 20582. The date is taken back off the trace's own x.
  # "pts" rather than "points" because a first game worth a single point would
  # otherwise read "1 points", and spelling it out for the twelve places that
  # happens would cost 56 KB. It is what the dossier's game bars already say.
  hover(
    "%{customdata[0]}<br>%{customdata[1]} · %{y:,} pts",
    custom = function(tr) {
      unname(Map(c, tr$key, short_date(as.Date(tr$x, origin = "1970-01-01"))))
    }
  )

```

# 2026 Playoffs

```{r playoff-card-helpers}
playoff_team_line <- function(team_id, series_wins, winner_id) {
  if (is.na(team_id)) {
    return(div(class = "ps-team pending", span(class = "ps-team-name", "TBD")))
  }
  team <- playoff_seeds |> filter(.data$team_id == .env$team_id)
  record <- post_team_records |> filter(.data$team_id == .env$team_id)
  detail <- if (nrow(record) == 0L) {
    "No playoff games"
  } else {
    sprintf("%d–%d · scores %.1f, allows %.1f per game",
            record$w, record$l, record$pf, record$pa)
  }
  div(
    class = paste("ps-team", if (!is.na(winner_id) && winner_id == team_id) "advanced"),
    style = paste0("--team:", team$color),
    div(class = "ps-team-top",
        if (is.na(team$logo)) NULL else
          tags$img(src = team$logo, alt = "", loading = "lazy"),
        span(class = "ps-seed", paste0("#", team$seed)),
        span(class = "ps-team-name", team$name),
        span(class = "ps-wins", series_wins)),
    div(class = "ps-team-detail", detail)
  )
}

playoff_series_card <- function(row) {
  status <- if (is.na(row$a_id) || is.na(row$b_id)) {
    "Pairing pending"
  } else if (!is.na(row$winner_id)) {
    "Series final"
  } else if (row$a_wins + row$b_wins > 0L) {
    "Series in progress"
  } else {
    "Series not started"
  }
  div(
    class = "ps-series",
    div(class = "ps-series-head",
        span(paste0("Series ", row$series_id)),
        span(paste0("Best of ", 2L * row$wins_needed - 1L))),
    playoff_team_line(row$a_id, row$a_wins, row$winner_id),
    playoff_team_line(row$b_id, row$b_wins, row$winner_id),
    div(class = "ps-series-status", status)
  )
}

playoff_stage <- function(title, rows) {
  div(
    class = "ps-stage",
    div(class = "ps-stage-title", title),
    div(class = "ps-stage-series",
        lapply(seq_len(nrow(rows)), \(i) playoff_series_card(rows[i, ])))
  )
}

playoff_leader <- function(col, label) {
  if (!post_has_games) return(playoff_empty())
  stat_card(stat_post_dfs[[col]], col, label)
}
```

```{r playoff-games}
#| title: Game schedule · where to watch
# The slider sits outside the table and sets a filter on the hidden `day`
# column through reactable's JavaScript API. The phone layout below is not a
# reactable, so the same handler hides its cards by their `data-day`.
playoff_day_js <- sprintf('
function psFromDay(value) {
  var day = Number(value);
  var labels = %s;
  document.getElementById("ps-day-value").textContent =
    day > 1 ? labels[day - 1] + " onward" : "All dates";
  Reactable.setFilter("playoff-games-table", "day", day > 1 ? day : undefined);
  document.querySelectorAll(".ps-game-mobile").forEach(function(card) {
    card.hidden = Number(card.dataset.day) < day;
  });
}', jsonlite::toJSON(playoff_days$day_label))

tagList(
  if (nrow(playoff_days) > 1) {
    div(
      class = "ps-day-filter",
      tags$label(`for` = "ps-day-slider", "Hide games before"),
      tags$input(
        id = "ps-day-slider", type = "range",
        min = 1, max = nrow(playoff_days), step = 1, value = 1,
        oninput = "psFromDay(this.value)"
      ),
      span(id = "ps-day-value", "All dates"),
      tags$script(HTML(playoff_day_js))
    )
  },
  playoff_schedule |>
    select(when, matchup, watch, round, series, game, result, day) |>
    reactable(
      elementId = "playoff-games-table",
      compact = TRUE,
      highlight = TRUE,
      striped = FALSE,
      rowClass = function(index) playoff_schedule$date_class[index],
      searchable = TRUE,
      defaultPageSize = 15,
      theme = court_theme,
      columns = list(
        when = colDef(name = "Date · ET", minWidth = 170, sortable = FALSE),
        matchup = colDef(name = "Game", minWidth = 220, sortable = FALSE),
        watch = colDef(
          name = "Watch", minWidth = 155, sortable = FALSE,
          html = TRUE,
          cell = function(value) markup(div(class = "ps-watch", value))
        ),
        round = colDef(name = "Round", minWidth = 95),
        series = colDef(name = "Series", minWidth = 100),
        game = colDef(name = "Number", minWidth = 125),
        result = colDef(name = "Result", minWidth = 100),
        day = colDef(
          show = FALSE,
          filterMethod = JS("function(rows, columnId, filterValue) {
            return rows.filter(function(row) {
              return row.values[columnId] >= filterValue
            })
          }")
        )
      )
    ),
  div(
    class = "ps-games-mobile",
    lapply(seq_len(nrow(playoff_schedule)), function(i) {
      game <- playoff_schedule[i, ]
      div(
        class = paste("ps-game-mobile", game$date_class),
        `data-day` = game$day,
        div(class = "ps-game-mobile-meta",
            span(game$when), span(paste(game$round, game$game, sep = " · "))),
        div(class = "ps-game-mobile-matchup", game$matchup),
        div(class = "ps-game-mobile-watch",
            span("Watch"), strong(game$watch)),
        div(class = "ps-game-mobile-result", game$result)
      )
    })
  ),
  div(class = "ps-source",
      "Watch listings: ESPN schedule and ",
      tags$a(href = "https://www.wnba.com/news/2026-wnba-postseason-faq",
             "WNBA postseason schedule", target = "_blank", rel = "noopener noreferrer"),
      ". Times and outlets may change. 'If necessary' games depend on series results.")
)
```

```{r experience}
  court_gg +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    aspect.ratio = court_ratio
  )

ggplotly(seasons_plot, tooltip = c("athlete", "n_seasons", "n_games")) |>
  highlight(
    color = "#ffffff",
    opacityDim = 0.35,
    selected = attrs_selected(marker = list(size = 12))
  ) |>
  basic_bundle() |>
  hover(
    "%{customdata[0]}<br>%{customdata[1]} over %{customdata[2]}",
    custom = function(tr) {
      unname(Map(c, tr$key, counted(tr$y, "game"), counted(tr$x, "season")))
    }
  )

```

## Row {height=110px}

::: {.card title="Where these careers begin"}
Every total on this page is regular season only, and the box scores start in
2004. The league started in 1997, so a career that opened before 2004 is
counted only from 2004 on: Sue Bird, Tamika Catchings, Lisa Leslie, Sheryl
Swoopes, Tina Thompson, Katie Smith and Lauren Jackson each played seasons this
page cannot see, and each sits below her official career line by exactly what
it cannot see. From 2004 on these match the league's own figures to within a
few tenths of a percent — that last fraction is games ESPN never filed a box
score for, 23 of them in 2004 alone. The Methods page has the detail.
:::

# Franchises

## Row

### Column {width=20%}

```{r champs}
#| title: "Champions"

reactable(
  champions,
  elementId = "champions",
  compact = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  sortable = FALSE,
  pagination = FALSE,
  theme = court_theme,
  # `rowClass` runs on every render and reads the meta the team cards set, so
  # the lit rows follow the filtering card rather than a moment in time. The
  # cards are two pages away now, and still reach this: every page of a Quarto
  # dashboard is one HTML document.
  rowClass = JS(
    "function(rowInfo, state) {
       if (!state.meta || !state.meta.team) { return null; }
       return rowInfo.values.franchise === state.meta.team ? 'champ-lit' : null;
     }"
  ),
  columns = list(
    season = colDef(name = "Season", maxWidth = md, style = list(color = mute)),
    champion = colDef(name = "Champion", minWidth = 150),
    # carried for the highlight to match on, never shown
    franchise = colDef(show = FALSE)
  )
)
```

### Column {width=80%}

```{r franchises}
#| fig-width: !expr lineage_fig_w
#| fig-height: !expr lineage_fig_h

# The one chart that still carries rasters: fifteen crests, embedded base64 in
# the SVG and base64'd again whole by `embed-resources`, which is 164 KB of its
# 240 KB. Still well under the 401 KB it came to as a 2x png, and the crests were
# being upscaled from their 96px source at 2x anyway.

# The dashboard's other two charts go through ggplotly because they answer the
# crosstalk selection. This one has nothing to answer -- no athlete is a
# franchise -- and ggplotly charges for the trip: it drops plot.subtitle
# silently, and it ignores a mapped hjust, which centred every label and ran
# the long ones off the left of the panel. Drawn straight, both work.
lineage_plot <- ggplot(franchises) +
  # Each era is its own line, stopped by a dot, so a rename reads as one era
  # arriving at its dot and the next setting off from it. Thin, so the row
  # belongs to the name rather than to the rule under it.
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = from, xend = end, y = row, yend = row, colour = I(colour)),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  # Under the marks that close a line rather than over them: a title won in the
  # last season of an era would otherwise cover the dot that says the era ended.
  geom_polygon(
    aes(x = x, y = y, group = title_id),
    data = stars, fill = gold, colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = end, y = row, colour = I(colour)),
    data = \(d) filter(era_ends, mark == "closed"),
    size = 2.1
  ) +
  # hollow, because 2026 is where the record stops and not where the club did
  geom_point(
    aes(x = end, y = row, colour = I(colour)),
    data = \(d) filter(era_ends, mark == "open"),
    size = 2.1, shape = 21, fill = ink, stroke = 0.7
  ) +
  # ESPN draws these crests for white paper, so the dark ones -- the Aces, the
  # Wings -- all but vanish on this page. A pale disc behind every one of them
  # gives back the background they were designed against, and reads as a badge
  # rather than as a patch over two special cases.
  geom_point(
    aes(x = end, y = row),
    # a border in the fill's own colour, not `colour = NA`: the filled shapes
    # are drawn as one path, and a missing border takes the fill with it
    data = crests, size = 6.4, shape = 21, fill = bone, colour = bone
  ) +
  # and the crest for every club still out there, one layer apiece because a
  # raster annotation takes one image and fixed corners, not a column of them
  pmap(crests, function(era, row, end, url, file, image) {
    annotation_raster(
      image,
      xmin = end - crest_seasons / 2, xmax = end + crest_seasons / 2,
      ymin = row - crest_rows / 2, ymax = row + crest_rows / 2,
      interpolate = TRUE
    )
  }) +
  # two layers rather than a mapped hjust, which ggplot takes only as a constant
  geom_text(
    aes(x = label_x, y = row + 0.45, label = era, colour = I(colour)),
    data = \(d) filter(d, !from_right),
    hjust = 0, size = lineage_size
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = label_x, y = row + 0.45, label = era, colour = I(colour)),
    data = \(d) filter(d, from_right),
    hjust = 1, size = lineage_size
  ) +
  # A tick for every season, because a star's year has to be readable off the
  # axis and a label every five years cannot do it. Only the fives are named:
  # thirty numbers along the bottom would be a wall to read past rather than a
  # scale to read from, and a minor tick draws at half the length of a major
  # one, which is the hierarchy said in the marks themselves.
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1997, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, last_season),
    minor_breaks = seq(1997, last_season, 1),
    guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.015)
  ) +
  # room above the top line for its label, which would otherwise sit on the frame
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Names and Places",
    subtitle = paste(
      "each line is one franchise · a break in it is a new name or a new city",
      "· a crest is a club still playing · a gold star is a title"
    ),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  court_gg +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 19, color = bone),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = mute),
    plot.margin = unit(c(18, 30, 14, 22), "points")
  )

lineage_plot

```
